en: Prosperity!
The Noble Root Manual of Mañjuśrī. Homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Thus have I heard:

At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling in a pavilion for the assembly of Bodhisattvas, which was inconceivable, marvelous, and wondrously arrayed, situated in the expanse of the sky above the Śuddhāvāsa heaven.
There, the Blessed One addressed the sons of the gods belonging to the Śuddhāvāsa host:

"Listen, O sons of the gods, to the inconceivable and miraculous display of the conduct, meditative absorption, purification, excellence, and liberation-circle of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, as well as his Bodhisattva-transformations."

I shall speak these mantra-words for the benefit of all sentient beings—words that sustain all beings with long life, health, sovereignty, and the fulfillment of their heart's desires, and which bring an end to evil.
Listen to them; attend well and thoroughly to them in your mind, and I shall speak them to you.

Then those sons of the gods belonging to the Śuddhāvāsa realm, with palms joined, [praised him] for the attainment of the special stages, the treading upon the Vajrāsana, the subduing of Māra, the turning of the wheel of Dharma, the departure of all Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, rebirth among gods and humans, the pacification of all suffering, the removal of poverty, sickness, and disease,
the non-surpassability of all mundane and supramundane mantra practices, the fulfillment of all hopes, and the unfailing retention of the words of all Tathāgatas.
Therefore, may the Blessed One, with a mind of loving-kindness and a mind of benefit, out of compassion for us and for all sentient beings, please speak.

Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni, having surveyed the entire realm of the Śuddhāvāsa heaven with his Buddha-eye, entered the samādhi called *Viśuddhaviṣayajyotirvikaraṇavidhvaṃsinī*. Immediately upon the Blessed One’s entry into that state, a ray of light named *Saṅkusumitabodhisattvasañcodanī* [issued forth]; and having seen the illumination of that white ray, [the assembly was moved].
Smiling slightly, he addressed that assembly of Bodhisattvas:
"O sons of the Conqueror, this is our summons by light;
come here!"
May you all prepare yourselves.
Then indeed, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, with eyes wide open and unblinking, stood facing the direction from which that radiance of light came.
Then that ray of light, having illuminated the world-system Kusumāvatī— the one that incites— with a great radiance, [approached] the Blessed One.
Having circumambulated the Tathāgata Saṅkusumitarājendra three times, it vanished into the crown of the head of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī.
Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, rising from his seat, circumambulated the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Saṅkusumitarājendra, three times; bowing his head in prostration,
he placed his right knee upon the ground.
He addressed the Blessed One, Saṅkusumitarājendra, as follows: "The Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śākyamuni, has taken us into his consideration.

O Blessed One, let us go from here to the Sahā world-system to see, pay homage to, and serve the Blessed One Śākyamuni, [and to receive] the ritual procedures for all mantra practices, accomplishments, and means, the mandala rites, the secret manuals, the cloth-painting rituals, the heart-essence of all Tathāgatas, the secret mudrās, and the consecrations."
To instruct all sentient beings and to fulfill all their aspirations.
When this had been said, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Saṅkusumitarājendra, spoke thus to Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta: "Go, Mañjuśrī Kumāra, at whatever time you deem appropriate.
Furthermore, in my name, the Blessed Śākyamuni should be asked whether he is free from ailment, free from distress, light in his movements, and dwelling in comfort."
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Saṅkusumitarājendra, said this to Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta:
"Furthermore, O Youth, [this has been taught] by Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksambuddhas as numerous as the sands of a hundred thousand Ganges rivers."

I shall now also speak of that which culminates in the practice [of the mantra], including the chapters on the secret empowerment of the maṇḍala for the practice of mantras, the ritual procedures for mudrās, fire offerings, recitations, and observances; that which fulfills all hopes and satisfies all sentient beings; the extensive chapter on the Jewel of Light; the sovereignty of the knowledge of the past, future, and present; the prophecy of lordship; the turning of mantras; the finality and conclusion of the place; the chapter on the dispersal at the time of the samaya of disappearance; and the complete and exhaustive traversal of all mundane and supramundane levels of the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, noble Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas.
"Go, Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, to express your approval; go now to the presence of Śākyamuni, face to face, whenever you deem it the right time. There you shall hear this Dharma discourse."
You too shall speak.
And there is a mantra for this occasion: *Namaḥ sarvatathāgatānām acintyāpratihatashāsanānām oṃ ra ra smara*.
O you who possess the form of a prince whose command is unimpeded, hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā!
O youth, this is that Mañjuśrī-mūlamantra;
it is the heart-essence of all Tathāgatas and has been spoken by all the Tathāgatas.
They shall speak it;
you too shall now speak it,
having gone to the Sahā world-system, in detail and with full analysis, as that which accomplishes all karmas.
It was authorized by the Tathāgata Śākyamuni.
Herein is the supreme heart-mantra: *oṃ vākye da namaḥ*.
And herein is the near-heart-mantra: *vākye hūṃ*.

Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, having been authorized by the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Saṅkusumitarāja, entered the samādhi called "Attaining the Seat of Awakening, which is the Outflow of the Bodhisattva Practice and the Array of All Ornaments. As soon as Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta had entered that samādhi, the entire expanse of all directions— the four quarters, the zenith, the nadir, and the intermediate points— was pervaded by the Blessed Buddhas.

That entire world-system became filled [with light]. "Excellent, excellent, O Son of the Conqueror! That you enter this distinguished samādhi is such that it cannot be accomplished even by all the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, or bodhisattvas who have entered the course of practice and are established in the ten stages."
The Tathāgata Saṅkusumitarājendra, having consulted together with those Blessed Buddhas, spoke this supreme heart-mantra of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, which is the most secret and accomplishes all aims.
Known as the "Single Syllable," it is supremely secret, brings benefit to all sentient beings, is divine, and is to be accomplished through other specific mantra practices as well.
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Saṅkusumitarājendra, remained silent for a moment.
Having surveyed the entire world-system with his Buddha-eye and having called to mind those Blessed Buddhas, he uttered the mantra with a mind characterized by loving-kindness:
"Homage to all Buddhas!"
This is the mantra, O Mañjuśrī; it is the supreme heart-mantra that accomplishes all activities.

Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, having arisen from that samādhi— just as a strong man might extend his bent arm or bend his extended arm— in a mere snap of the fingers, in a moment no longer than the blink of an eye, he, whose intellect was born of the power and strength of purity, entered the specific miraculous transformation of the samādhi called "The Summoning" and returned to this Sahā world-system.
Having arrived, he stationed himself above in the realm of the Śuddhāvāsa devas, which rests upon great maṇi-jewels in the expanse of the sky.
Having illuminated that entire abode of the Śuddhāvāsas with a great radiance of light rays, he entered the meditative absorption named "Illumination Adorned with Luminous Jewels."

Immediately upon entering meditative absorption, Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta manifested for the purpose of honoring the Blessed One Śākyamuni a divine rain of perfumes, garlands, ointments, wreaths, and powders; as well as a celestial palace composed of many jewels, adorned with jeweled parasols extending for hundreds of thousands of yojanas, beautified by divine visible arrays of fine silk cloths, and filled with divine flowers, banners, flags, and garlands, bound together by nets of jeweled bells that produced a sweet sound proclaiming the non-retrogression and establishment of bodhisattvas.
Having seen that marvelous, wondrous miracle, the miraculous transformation of the Bodhisattva.

Then those sons of the gods belonging to the Śuddhāvāsa realm, their hair standing on end with joy, saw their abode trembling; with hearts agitated and broken, wondering "Have we perhaps fallen away from our supernatural power?", they began to cry out loudly in great haste, saying: "Save us, Blessed One! Save us, Śākyamuni!"
Then the Blessed One addressed the entire assembly of the Śuddhāvāsa deities:
"Do not fear, friends; do not be afraid!
This is that Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, [who dwells] in the Buddha-field Saṅkusumita, [the realm] of the Tathāgata Saṅkusumitarāja."

He has come into the presence of the Tathāgata to see him, to pay homage to him, and to attend upon him, and to have explained the vast and marvelous Dharma-discourse concerning the great practice of meaningful conduct and the words of mantras.

Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, having circumambulated the Blessed One Śākyamuni three times, gazed at the Blessed One with unblinking eyes, prostrated at his feet, and praised the Blessed One with these syllables and phrases:
"Homage to you, the liberated one, O noble one! Homage to you, the supreme among men!
Homage to you, the best of beings, the accomplisher of the purpose of all conduct! (Mmk 1.1)
Homage to you, O lion among men, the warder-off of all misfortunes!
May your mind be gracious, O great hero, the destroyer of all difficulties.
Homage to you, O Puruṣa, whose holy fragrance is like that of a lotus, O infinite one!
Homage to you, O Puruṣa-lotus, who purifies the mire of the three worlds!
Homage to you, the liberated one, the deliverer from all suffering;
homage to you, the peaceful one, the perfect subduer of all who are unsubdued.
Homage to you, the Siddha, who accomplishes the purpose of all mantra practices;
homage to you, the auspicious one, the most auspicious of all auspicious things.
Homage to you, the Buddha, who has awakened to all phenomena;
homage to you, the Tathāgata, who is the suchness of all phenomena,
O Teacher who has entered into the mode of non-proliferation.

"Salutations to you, the All-Knowing One, who are established in the establishment of the objects of all-knowledge—both conditioned and unconditioned—the three vehicles, the path, and nirvāṇa. By means of these syllables, phrases, summaries, and verses of praise, [he] addressed the Blessed One face-to-face... [having passed beyond] world-systems in the northeast.
In a certain direction there was a buddha-field named Saṅkusumita.

Therein was a world-system called Kusumāvatī, where that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Saṅkusumitarājendra— the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct— dwells and teaches the Dharma that is good in the beginning, [good in the middle, and good in the end].
He fully revealed the Buddha’s conduct, which is virtuous in the beginning, virtuous in the middle, and virtuous in the end; it is beneficial, entirely complete, pure, and purified for all people.

He now stands, remains, and maintains himself, and he teaches the Dharma— which is a protection, a shelter, a refuge, and a final resort, a state of security, the ultimate goal, and the ultimate consummation— for the sake of all sentient beings.

Having been granted permission by that very Blessed One, he has come here to the presence of the Blessed One’s feet; and that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Saṅkusumitarājendra, inquired after the Blessed One’s freedom from illness, ease of movement, vigor, and well-being, and spoke thus: "It is marvelous indeed that in such a time of the five corruptions, the Buddha, the Blessed One Śākyamuni, has appeared and teaches all dharmas."
With its words and syllables complete and flawless, it brings about the attainment of the three paths, liberation, and rebirth among gods and humans.
How marvelous is the heroic vigor of that Blessed One, Śākyamuni!
For he establishes beings—who are indeed unfit, following a path that leads to the arising of the three realms of existence—firmly in Nirvana, which follows the ultimate security and well-being.
Moreover, O Blessed One, only the Blessed Buddhas themselves will know the mind of the Blessed Buddhas.

What is it possible for me to know of the Blessed Ones’ inconceivable, marvelous, and wondrous miraculous transformations—the Buddha-transformations—or to know their mental conduct, their practice, their entry [into reality], their accomplishment, and their activities? Even in a hundred thousand nayutas of kotis of eons, how could one describe them even in brief?
This manifestation of the Tathāgatas, in its entirety and in its parts through all forms, is to be viewed as a conditioned phenomenon (*saṃskṛtadharma*).
Regarding the conduct of those who rely on the ancient [teachings] to be abandoned by vision, or their qualities to be proclaimed, only the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, knows this; we do not.
Then Mañjuśrī, the Youthful Prince, seated upon a great jewel-lotus created through the miraculous transformations of his own supernatural power,
gazed upon the Blessed One Śākyamuni.
Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī, the Youthful Prince, following a discourse on various topics.

Having become a Tathāgata, he addressed Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta with a Brahma-like voice— one that preceded his former questions and was accompanied by the purpose of accomplishing the bodhisattva conduct conducive to the teaching of the Dharma— a voice possessing the resonance of a kalaviṅka’s song, the thundering of a cloud, and the sounding of a drum.

Welcome to you, Mañjuśrī, Great Being! You who have accomplished the conduct empowered by all Buddhas; you who bring about the welfare of all Bodhisattvas; you who possess the secret empowerment, mudrās, and mandalas of all mantra-words; you who fulfill all hopes for longevity, health, and sovereignty; you who provide the knowledge of the tantras and the objects of knowledge necessary for all accomplishments; you who bestow kingdoms, fields, and the preservation of the past, future, and present; in short, you who fulfill all the hopes of all sentient beings, awakening their own virtues and causing joy in other beings through the practice of mantra-conduct.
It effects invisibility, travel through the sky, movement by foot, the making of one wise, summoning, entry into the netherworld (pātāla), and sorcery;

it is crowded with the attainment of all desires, and it summons yakṣas, yakṣiṇīs, servants (kiṅkara), piśācas, and all spirits; it restores children, the elderly, and the young to their original state;
in short, it performs all rites, fulfills all heart's wishes, and is employed in sorcery, pacification, and nourishment.
Just as it is being applied and just as it is being heard, this *Mahākalparatnapaṭalavisara*, the crest-jewel of the Bodhisattvapiṭaka,

has been authorized by us and by all the Buddhas for the sake of pure beings— for the benefit of many, for the happiness of many, and for the sake of all beings, both gods and humans— this treasury of Dharma.
Then, indeed, Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta entered the bodhisattva-samādhi called "The Array of the Radiance-Beams of the Empowerment of All Buddhas, Which Provokes Adornment.

Immediately upon his entering it, [the light reached] as far as many Ganges rivers... up to the world-system and as far as the great Avīci hell; whatever beings there were who were suffering intensely—
They all attained the peace that extinguishes suffering.
Having exhorted all the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and Blessed Buddhas, that ray of light once again vanished into the crown of the head of the bodhisattva Mañjuśrī.
In the meantime, as for those buddha-fields situated in the eastern direction...
There, the Buddha Bhagavāns were impelled by that manifestation of the radiance of the circle of light-rays;
namely, the Tathāgata named Jyotiḥsaumyagandhāvabhāsaśrī.
The Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguruvaiḍūryaprabharāja, the Tathāgata named Samantāvabhāsaśrī, the Tathāgata named Samudgatarāja, and the Tathāgata named Śālendrarāja.
The Tathāgata named Lokendrarāja, the Tathāgata named Amitāyurjñānaviniścayarāja,
and the Tathāgata named Anantāvabhāsarājendra.

The Tathāgata named Jyotiraśmirājendra— these and other Buddhas, Blessed Ones, surrounded by hosts of bodhisattvas, as well as the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas in infinite and boundless world-systems, [all gazed upon] Śākyamuni residing in the Śuddhāvāsa heaven within the Sahā world-system.

The Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, together with Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, were expounding the detailed chapters on the meaning of the mantra words for the exposition of the bodhisattva conduct; those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, gathered there from the south, the west, the north, and from all the cardinal and intermediate directions.

Thus, having illuminated all the Buddha-fields above, below, and across, and having humbled all the abodes of Māra in every Buddha-field, they— surrounded by hosts of Bodhisattvas and preceded by the community of Śrāvakas— desiring to display the palace of the Pure Abodes, the miraculous transformations of the Buddhas, and the majesty of the Bodhisattvas, [proclaimed] the unimpeded teaching of the Tathāgata, which consists of the extensive chapters on the specific samādhis for accomplishing the practice of mantras.
Desiring to illuminate [the meaning], they stood forth; namely—
Subāhu, Suratna, and so on.
Suvrata, Sunetra, Sūrata.
Sudharmā, Sarvārthasiddhi, Sarvodgata,
Dharmodgata, Ratnodgata, and Ratnaśrī.
Meruśrī, Acintyaśrī, and Prabhākaraśrī.
Prabhaśrī, Jyotiśrī, Sarvārthaśrī,
Sarvaratnapāṇi, Cūḍāmaṇi, and Merudhvajapāṇi.
Vairocanagarbha, Ratnagarbha, and Jñānagarbha.
The womb of inconceivable meaning, the womb of the inconceivable meaning, and the womb of the Dharma-ascending.
Dhvajaketu, Suketu, and Anantaketu.
Vimalaketu, Gaganaketu, Ratnaketu,
Garjitaghoṣadundubhisvararāja, Anantāvabhāsajñānarāja,
and Sarvatamo’ndhakāravidhamanarāja.
Sarvavikiraṇabodhividhvaṃsanarāja, Sarvacaryātiśayajñānarāja, Lokendrarāja.
Atiśayendrarāja, Vidhamanarāja, Nirdhūtarāja,
Ādityarāja,
Abhāvasamudgatarāja, and Svabhāvasamudgatarāja.
King Arisen from the Nature of Non-existence, King Beyond Discourse,
Radiance of the Merit of Essential Nature.
Lokābha, Amitābha, and Mitābha.
Resplendent as the sun,
resplendent as the moon,
resplendent with the nature of reality.
Unassailable, unendurable, and irremovable.
Akaniṣṭha,
Amala, Anala.
Dyutimat, Patimat, Sukhamukha, Nemi, Nimikeṭu, Ṛkṣa, Divideva, Divyanābhi, Ravaṇa, Lokaśānti, Upāriṣṭa, Dundubhisiddha, Śiva, Ākhyadivya, Duprasaha, Durgharṣa, Durālabha, Dūraṅgama,
Durālabha, Dūrasthita, Ūrdhvadravyatama, Khadyotasama, Hadyota, Adyota, Ṛṣabha, Ābha, Sumanāya, and Sumana.

Mahādeva, Sunirmala, Malānta, Dānta, Sami, Sucihna, Śvetadhvaja, Imi, Kimi, Kaniṣṭha, Nikarṣa, Jīva, Sujāta, Dhūmaketu, Dhvajaketu, Śvetaketu, Suketu, Vasuketu, Vasava, Pitāmaha, Pitara, Niṣka, Kuruloka, Samanta, Mahākhya.

Śreyas, Tejas, Jyotikiraṇa, Samantakara, Lokāṅkara, Divāṅkara, Dīpaṅkara, Bhūtāntakara, Sarvārthāṅkara, Siddhāṅkara, Dyotyaṅkara, Avabhāsāṅkara, Dundubhisvara, Rutasvara, Susvara, Anantasvara, Ketusvara, Bhūtamuni, Kanakamuni, Krakucchanda, Kāśyapa, Śikhin, Viśvabhuk, Vipaśyin, and Śākyamuni.
Then, having illuminated that abode of the Pure Abodes with these and many other Blessed Buddhas, and having seated themselves upon lotus thrones,
they addressed the assembly of Bodhisattvas and the gods of the earth in this manner: "Such is the form [of this teaching]."
Namely: Ratnapāṇi,
Vajrapāṇi, and Supāṇi.
Anantapāṇi, Kṣitipāṇi, Ālokapāṇi, Sunirmala, Sukūpa, Prabhūtakūṭa, Maṇikūṭa, Ratnakūṭa, Ratnahasti, Samantahasti, Gandhahasti, Sugati, Vimalagati, Lokagati, Cārugati, Anantagati, Anantakīrti,
Vimalakīrti, Gatikīrti, Amalakīrti, Kīrtikīrti, Nātha, Anātha, Nāthabhūta, Lokanātha, Samantanātha.
Ātreya, Anantatreya, Samantatreya, Maitreya, Sunetreya, Namantatreya, Tvaddhatreya, Sarūlātreya,
Trirantātreya, Triśaraṇātreya, Triyānātreya, Visphūrja, Sumanodbhavarṇavān, Dharmīśvara, Abhāveśvara.
Sammateśvara, Lokeśvara,
Avalokiteśvara.

O Lord who beholds the world, O Lord who surveys the world, O Great One, the most great, O Lord of the roar, O Lord with the sound of a drum, O Lord of the vast expanse, O Lord who has shattered [all bonds], O One of beautiful chest, O One of beautiful form, O You possessed of very great fame, O You with the power of the sun, O Radiant One, O Lord of the moon,
O Moon-like, O Gentle One, O Infinite Glory, O Glory of the World, O Sky, O One enriched by the sky, O Lord of the sky-goer, O Great Lord, O Dweller on Earth, O Womb of the Earth.
Nīvaraṇa, Sarvāvaraṇa, Sarvāvaraṇaviṣkambhin, Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin, Samantanirmathana,
Samantabhadra, Bhadrapāṇi, Sudhana, Susaṃhata, Rasapuṣya, Sunabha, Ākāśa, Ākāśagarbha, Sarvārthagarbha, Sarvodbhava, Anivartin, Anivartita, Apāyajaha, Avivartita, and Avaivarttikasarvadharmopaśānti.
Together with these and other bodhisattva mahāsattvas, the Blessed One Śākyamuni was dwelling in the abode of the Śuddhāvāsa gods.

There were also other Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who had assumed the forms of women; by means of infinite conduct, purpose, and worldly engagement, they established all beings upon the path of non-retrogression according to their inclinations. They possessed inconceivable bases of ignorance, mantras, dhāraṇīs, and medicinal herbs, and they assumed various forms and appearances. They entered into the company of diverse flocks of birds, yakṣas, rākṣasas, jewels, mantras, and kings of gems—whether reckoned as sentient beings or non-sentient—and followed the conduct of beings. They acted in accordance with the dispositions of beings in order to discipline them according to their respective inclinations.

[They were] those who followed forms distinguished by that [teaching], who had emerged from the Dharma through the correct understanding of the instructions of the Vidyārājas, who entered into all mundane and supramundane realms by means of the Tathāgata-lotus and -vajra, who established the path of speech that cannot be transgressed regarding the *samaya*, and who ensured the non-interruption of the lineage of the Three Jewels—
namely: Uṣṇīṣa, Atyadbhuta, Atyunnata, Sitātapatra, Anantapatra, Śatapatra, Jayoṣṇīṣa, Lokottara, Vijayoṣṇīṣa,
Abhyudgatoṣṇīṣa, Kamalaraśmi, Kanakaraśmi, Sitaraśmi, and Vyūḍhoṣṇīṣa.

The Heap of Gold, the Heap of Silver, the Heap of Radiance, the Heap of Jewels, the Heap of Equality, the Renowned Heap, the Heap of Beings, the Heap of Truth, the Heap of the Nature of Non-existence, the Heap of the Unfailing— by these and other Uṣṇīṣa Kings who have entered the infinite realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), who fulfill the aspirations and intentions of sentient beings according to their inclinations,
and who have arrived from all directions at the heart of all Victors, it is not possible even in hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of eons [to describe] the Uṣṇīṣa Kings.
It is impossible to state the limit of their number or to describe the majesty of those whose strength and prowess are inconceivable; therefore,
it is spoken of here by way of a brief indication and in summary.
The assembly of the Queen of Vidyās shall now be described.
It is as follows: Ūrṇā, Bhrūlocanā, Padmā, Śravaṇā, Grīvā, Abhayā, Karuṇā, Maitrī, Kṛpā, Prajñā, Raśmi, Cetanā, Prabhā, Nirmalā, and Dhīvarā.
Likewise, there were other Vidyārājñīs emanated from the infinite and boundless forms of the Tathāgatas,
namely: Tathāgatapātra, Dharmacakra, Tathāgataśayana, Tathāgatāvabhāsa, Tathāgatavacana, Tathāgatoṣṭha, Tathāgatoru, Tathāgatāmala, Tathāgata-dhvaja, Tathāgata-ketu, and Tathāgata-cinha.

And by these and other Vidyārājas, Rājñīs, Kiṅkaras, Ceṭas, Ceṭīs, Dūtas, Dūtīs, Yakṣas, and Yakṣīs— spoken by the Tathāgata, emerged from the clouds of Dharma characterized by exceptionally magnificent arrays, flowing forth as the natural outpourings of specific meditative absorptions, accompanied by retinues of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions, and moving one above the other within the entire host of Vidyās.
They too were established there in the palace of the Śuddhāvāsa deities,
as well as the Vidyārājas of the Lotus family (Abjakula),
namely: the Blessed One with twelve arms, the one with six arms, the one with four arms, Hālāhala, Amoghapāśa, and White Hayagrīva.

Sugrīva, Anantagrīva, Nīlagrīva, Sugrīva, Sukarṇa, Śvetakarṇa, Nīlakaṇṭha, Lokakaṇṭha, Vilokita, Avalokita, Īśvara, Sahasraraśmi, Manaḥ, Manasaḥ, Vikhyātamanasaḥ, Kamala, Kamalapāṇi, Manoratha, Āśvāsaka, Prahasita, Sukeśa, Keśānta, Nakṣatra, Nakṣatrarāja, Saumya, Sugata, and Damaka.

And by these and other vidyārājas, headed by Abja-uṣṇīṣa, who have become the outflow of the samādhis of the infinite accomplishment of the clouds of Dharma, surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of lamps, and by many vidyārājñīs emanated from the samādhi of the form of Lokeśvara—
namely: Tārā, Sutārā, Naṭī, Bhṛkuṭī, Anantaṭī, Lokaṭī, Bhūmiprāpaṭī, Vimalaṭī, Sitā, and Śvetā.
Mahāśvetā, Pāṇḍaravāsinī, Lokavāsinī, Vimalavāsinī, Abjavāsinī, Daśabalavāsinī, Yaśovatī, Bhogavatī, Mahābhogavatī, Ulūkā, Alokā, Amalāntakarī, Samantāntakarī, Duḥkhāntakarī, Bhūtāntakarī,
Śriyā, Mahāśriyā, Bhūpaśriyā, Anantaśriyā, Lokaśriyā, Vikhyātaśriyā, Lokamātā, Samantamātā.

Buddhamātā, Bhaginī, Bhāgīrathī, Surathī, Rathavatī, Nāgadantā, Damanī, Bhūtavatī, Amitā, Āvalī, Bhogavalī, Ākarṣaṇī, Adbhutā, Raśmī, Surasā, Suravatī, Pramodā, Dyutivatī, Taṭī, Samantataṭī, Jyotsnā, Somā,
Somāvatī, Māyūrī, Mahāmāyūrī, Dhanavatī, Dhanandadā, Suravatī, Lokavatī, Arciṣmatī.

Bṛhannalā, Bṛhaṃtā, Sughoṣā, Sunandā, Vasudā, Lakṣmī, Lakṣmīvatī, Rogāntikā, Sarvavyādhicikitsanī, Asamā, the Goddess Khyātikarī, Vaśakarī, Kṣiprakarī, Kṣemadā, Maṅgalā, Maṅgalāvahā, Candrā, Sucandrā, and Candrāvatī;
and with these and other queen-consorts of vidyās, headed by Parṇāsavari, Jāṅgulī, and Mānasī— whose nature is the infinite accomplishment of the dharmadhātu and the sky.

With minds generated by the empowerment of the miraculous transformations of the conduct of sentient beings, there were male and female messengers, male and female servants, male and female attendants, male and female yakṣas, male and female rākṣasas, and male and female piśācas, who, investigating the mantras for entering the samaya of the Lotus family, proceeded toward that Śuddhāvāsa celestial palace inhabited by pure beings.
Thereupon, he established himself;
and having established himself, we remained with our minds intent upon performing acts of worship for the Blessed One Śākyamuni.

In the presence of the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi addressed his own assembly of vidyās: "Gather together, sirs, surrounded by our assembly of vidyās, along with the wrathful kings, the vidyārājas, the vidyārājñīs, and the great messengers! At the mere thought of him, all the assemblies of vidyās gathered together.
They were as follows: Vidyottama, Suvidya, Suviddha, Subāhu, Suṣeṇa, Surāntaka, Surada, Supūrṇa, Vajrasena, Vajrakara,
Vajrabāhu, Vajrahasta, Vajradhvaja, Vajrapatāka, Vajraśikhara, Vajraśikha, Vajradaṃṣṭra, Śuddhavajra, Vajraroma, Vajrasaṃhata, Vajrānana, Vajrakavaca, Vajragrīva, Vajranābhi, and Vajrānta.
Vajra-enclosure, vajra-fortification, vajra-arrow, vajra-bow, vajra-shaft, vajra-nārāca,

vajra-marked, vajra-chain, vajra-underworld, vajra-terrible, + + + eye, vajra-wrath, moving at the end of water, moving at the end of spirits, moving at the end of odors, moving at the end of great wrath, moving at the end of Maheśvara, moving at the end of all vidyās, the terrible, the very terrible, the hurler, the secondary hurler.
The one who casts down with his footstep, the one who casts down the Vināyakas, the one who casts down with his placement, the one who casts down the preeminent, Bala, Mahābala, Sumbha, Bhramara,

Bhṛṅgiriṭi, Krodha, Mahākrodha, Sarvakrodha, Ajara, Ajagara, Jvara, Śoṣa, Nāgānta, Daṇḍa, Nīladaṇḍa, Raktāṅga, Vajradaṇḍa, Medhya, Mahāmedhya, Kāla, Kālakūṭa, Śvitraroma, and the destroyer of all beings.
Śūla, Mahāśūla, Ārti, Mahārti, Yama Vaivasvata, the bringer of the end of the age, the terrible one of the dark fortnight, the one of fearsome form, the crusher with the *paṭṭiśa*,
*tomara*, and club, the devourer, the one who destroys the cycle of existence, the sun at the end of the age, the taker of life, the slayer of Śakra, Dveṣa, Āmarṣa,
Kuṇḍalin, Sukuṇḍalin, Amṛtakuṇḍalin, Anantakuṇḍalin, Ratnakuṇḍalin, Bāhu, Mahābāhu.
[They are] the devourers of great diseases, malignant serpents, erysipelas, leprosy, and complications; they are insatiable and withering.

Together with these and other Vidyārājas and Great Krodhas, they are the subduers of all beings without exception, the ones who perform expulsion, destruction, bursting, killing, and annihilation, and the bestowers [of boons] upon those who are devoted.
Those who employ [these mantras] in rites of pacification, enrichment, and subjugation,

surrounded by hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of vidyārājas, gaze upon the Blessed One Śākyamuni and Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, while paying homage to their own vidyārāja Kuliśapāṇi and awaiting his command.
They remained in their respective places and sat down upon their individual seats.

Those great female messengers (mahādūtī) of the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi, together with their retinues of hundreds of thousands of millions of vidyārājñīs, also assembled at that place, having relied upon their own dharmadhātu, which is by nature movement and free from conceptual proliferation (niṣprapañca).
They were as follows: Mekhalā, Sumekhalā, Siṅkalā, Vajrārṇā, Vajrajihvā, Vajrabhrū, Vajralocanā, and Vajrāṃsā.
Vajrabhṛkuṭī, Vajraśravaṇā, Vajralekhā, Vajrasūcī, Vajramuṣṭī, Vajrāṅkuśī, Vajraśāṭī, Vajrāsanī,
Vajraśṛṅkhalā, Sālavatī, Sālāviraṭī, Kāminī, Vajrakāminī, Kāmavajriṇī, Paśyikā, Paśyinī,
Mahāpaśyinī, Śikharavāsinī, Grahilā, Dvāravāsinī, Kāmavajriṇī, Manojavā, Atijavā, and Śīghrajavā.
Sulocanā, Surasavatī, Bhramarī, Bhrāmarī, Yātrā, Siddhā, Anilā, Pūrā, Keśinī, Sukeśā, Hiṇḍinī, Tarjinī, Dūtī, Sudūtī, Māmakī, Vāmanī, Rūpiṇī, Rūpavatī, Jayā, Vijayā,
Ajitā, Aparājitā, Śreyasī, Hāsinī, Hāsavajriṇī, Lokavatī, Yaśavatī, Kuliśavatī, Adāntā, Trailokyavaśaṅkarī, Daṇḍā, Mahādaṇḍā.
They are Priyavādinī, Saubhāgyavatī, Arthavatī, Mahānarthā, Tittirī, Dhavalatittirī, Dhavalā, Sunirmitā,
Sunirmalā, Ghaṇṭā, Khaḍgapaṭṭisā, Sūcī, Jayatī, Aparā, Nirmitā, Nāyikā, Guhyakī, Visrambhikā, Musalā, and Sarvabhūtavaśaṅkarī.
These and other great female messengers, surrounded by a retinue of many hosts of female messengers, shall assemble right here in this great circle of the assembly.

And there are many *dhāraṇīs* arising from a mind cultivated by the outflow of meditative concentration (*samādhi-niṣyanda*), which take delight in the magical power of punishment for subduing wicked beings,
such as: the *vajrānalapramohanī* *dhāraṇī*, the *meruśikharakūṭāgāradhāriṇī*, the *ratnaśikharakūṭāgāradharaṇindharā*,
the *sukūṭā*, the *bahukūṭā*, the *puṣpakūṭā*, the *daṇḍadhāriṇī*, the *nigrahadhāraṇī*, and the *ākarṣaṇadhāriṇī*.
Keyūrā, Keyūravatī, Dhvajāgrakeyūrā, Ratnāgrakeyūrā, Lokāgrakeyūrā, Patāgrakeyūrā, Viparivartā, Lokāvartā, Sahasrāvartā, Vivasvāvartā, Sarvabhūtāvartā, Ketuvatī, Ratnavatī, Maṇiratnacūḍā,
Boddhyagā, Balavatī, Anantaketu, Samantaketu, Ratnaketu, Vikhyātaketu, Sarvabhūtaketu, and Ajiravatī.
Asvarā, Sunirmalā, Ṣaṇmukhā, Vimalā, and Lokākhyā—
these and many other hundreds of thousands of millions of dhāraṇīs, accompanied by their retinues, gathered together in that very great assembly circle.
There was also the empowerment of infinite Buddhas and the empowerment of the samādhis of the great bodhisattvas.
Then there are the Blessed Pratyekabuddhas who dwell in Buddha-fields devoid [of Buddhas], who are like the rhinoceros horn, wandering alone in the forest;

they act for the benefit of sentient beings, revealing the guidance of the Dharma through the practice of silence and patient endurance. Following the course of saṃsāra, their minds are ever-weary, their mental continuums are turned toward great compassion, and their volitions are preceded by and thoroughly cultivated by the bodhicitta that is itself refined solely by mental impressions (*cittavāsanā*).

Those whose minds have not turned toward the Bodhisattva stages— ranging from the first stage, the second, the third, up to the eighth— who possess weary minds and are terrified by the fear of saṃsāra,
they too would not assemble in this great circle of the assembly.
They were as follows: Gandhamādana, Sīmanta, Āyatana, Samantaprabha, Candana, Kāla, Upakāla, Nemi, Upanemi, Riṣṭa, Upariṣṭa, Upāriṣṭa, Pārśva, Supārśva, Dundubhi, Upadundubhi, Lokākhya,
Lokaprabha, Jayanta, Areṇu, Reṇu, Upareṇu, Aṃśa, Upāṃśa, Cihna, Sucihna, Dinakara, Sukara, and Prabhāvanta.
Prabhākara, Lokakara, Viśruta, Suśruta, Sukānta, Sudhānta, Sudānta, Adantānta, Bhavānta, Sitaketu, Jihmaketu, Ketu, Upaketu, Tathya, Padmahara, Padmasambhava, Svayambhu, Adbhuta,
Manoja, Manasa, Mahendrukūṭākhya, Kumbhasakalākhya, Makara, Upakara, Śānta, Śāntamānasa, Varma, Upavarma.
Vairocana, Kusuma, Sulīla, Śreya, Badhya-harāntaka, Duḥprasaha, Kanaka-vimalaketu, Soma, Susoma, Suṣeṇa, Sucīrṇa, Śukra, Kratu-iṣṭa, Upendra, and Vasu—

by these and by hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of other Pratyekabuddhas, who were inconceivable, incomparable, established in the middle vehicle that has entered the unconditioned, free from conceptual proliferation, whose nature is like the sky, and who have resolved upon the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu)— [this was taught].
The Blessed One Śākyamuni dwelt together with those who were free from the obstruction of grasping and aversion.
And with a great community of śrāvakas, accompanied by a retinue of many hundreds of thousands of koṭis of śrāvakas,
as follows: Mahākāśyapa, Nadīkāśyapa, Gayākāśyapa, Duravikṣokāśyapa, Bharadvāja, Viṇḍola,
Maudgalyāyana, Mahāmaudgalyāyana, Śāriputra, Mahāśāriputra, Subhūti, Mahāsubhūti, and Gavāmpati.
Kātyāyana, Mahākātyāyana, Upāli, Bhadrika, Kaphiṇa, Nanda, Ānanda, Sundarananda, Lokabhūta, Anantabhūta, Varṇaka, Upavarṇaka, Nandika, Upanandika, Aniruddha, Pūrṇa, Supūrṇa, Upapūrṇa, Tiṣya,
Punarvasu, Rūha, Raurava, Kuru, Pañcika, Upapañcika, Kāla, Sukāla, Devala, Rāhula, and Harita.

Upaharita, Dhyāyin, Nandīdhyāyika, Upāyi, Upayāyika, Śreyasaka, Dravya, Mallaputra, Upadravya, Upeta, Khaṇḍa, Tiṣya, Mahātiṣya, Samantatiṣya, Āhvaya, Nayasyoda, Yasika, Dhanika, Dhanavarṇa, Upadhanika,
Pilindavaśa, Pippala, Kimphala, Upaphala, Anantaphala, Saphala, Kumāra, and Kumārakāśyapa.
Mahoda, Ṣoḍaśavartikā, Nanda, Upananda, Jihva, Jihma, Jitapāśa, Maheṣvāsa, Vātsīka, Kurukulla, Upakurukulla, Koṭīkarṇa, Śramaṇa, Śroṇīparāntaka, Gāṅgeyaka, Girikarṇika, Koṭikarṇika, Vārṣika,
Jeta, Sujeta, Śrīgupta, Lokagupta, Gurugupta, Guruka, Dyotīrasa, Sanaka, Ḍimbhaka, and Upaḍimbhi.
Viśakoṭika, Anāthada, Uparitana, Vivartana, Unmattaka, Dyota, Samantabhadra, Suprabuddha, Svāgata, Upāgata,
Lohāgata, Duḥkhānta, Bhadrakalpika, Mahābhadrika, Arthacara, Pitāmaha, Gatika, Puṣpamāla, Puṣpakāśikha, Upakāśika, Mahauṣadha, Mahojaska, Mahoja, Anurādhamahaujaska, Mahoja, Anurādha.
Rādhaka, Rāsika, Subrahma, Suśobhana, Suloka, and Samāgama—

along with these and others who have tasted the flavor of liberation within the infinite realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), who have attained the single vehicle through the performance of the duties of the convergence of the three vehicles,

who have fled from *saṃsāra*, who meditate upon the three liberations and the four dhyānas, and who are perfectly concentrated, endowed with the four bases of miraculous power and the seven factors of enlightenment.
Together with those who were fully ordained— those who had entered the method [of practice] and had converged into the realm of nirvāṇa, being equal and free from conceptual proliferation—
he remained for three moments within that great circle of the assembly and before the Blessed One Śākyamuni;
immediately after the ten stages, they too sat down there.

And with many great female disciples who had entered the realm of nirvāṇa through the assembly, who relied upon the vehicle of the unconditioned ultimate, who were pure and free from passion, who had attained universal radiance, who purified the qualities of the field of those worthy of offerings, who were the very essence and ornament of sentient beings, and who were sovereigns over the world— sovereigns over all beings, whether two-footed, four-footed, many-footed, or footless, and a field of merit for gods and humans to be honored— such as Yaśodharā, Yaśodā, Mahāprajāpatī, and Prajāpatī.

Sujātā, Nandā, Sthūlanandā, Sunandā, Dhyāyinī, Sundarī, Anantā, Viśākhā, Manorathā, Jayavatī, Vīrā, Upavīrā, Devatā, Sudevatā, Āśritā, Śriyā, Pravarā, Pramuditā, Priyaṃvadā, Rohiṇī, Dhṛtarāṣṭrā, Dhṛtā, Svāmikā, Sampadā,
Vapuṣā, Śuddhā, Premā, Jaṭā, Upajaṭā, Samantajaṭā, Bhavāntikā, and Bhāvatī.

Manojavā, Keśavā, Viṣṇulā, Viṣṇuvatī, Sumanā, Bahumatā, Śreyasī, Duḥkhāntā, Karmadā, [Kāmadā], Vasudā, Dharmadā, Narmadā, Tāmrā, Sutāmrā, Kīrtivatī, Manovatī, Prahasitā, Tribhavāntā, Trimalāntā, Duḥkhaśāyikā, Nirvīṇā, Triparṇā, Padmavarṇā, Padmāvatī, Padmaprabhā, Padmā, Padmāvatī.
Triparṇī, Saptavarṇī, and Utpalavarṇā—
these and other great, most eminent female disciples approached the feet of the Blessed One to pay him homage.
Desiring to manifest the great maṇḍala of the Great Seeking and the miraculous transformations of the great bodhisattvas, they assembled and took their seats.
I became desirous of hearing the Dharma in order to illuminate the accomplishment of the purpose of mantra practice.

Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni, having gazed upon that entire circle of the assembly, with a pure and resolute intention, and having understood that the realm of sentient beings has the nature of non-existence, the nature of space, and transcends the three periods of time, addressed Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta: "Pay heed, Mañjuśrī, to the conduct for the benefit of sentient beings, which brings about the attainment of the purpose of mantra practice through the possession of faith in the desired fruits of action and the delighting in their respective inclinations."
Cultivate the bodhisattva samādhi named *Nāmāmadharmapadakarmapada-śāntipada-mokṣapada-kalpanirhāra-nirvikalpasamatāprāpaṇa-daśatathāgatabalasamantabala-sabala-mārabalābhivardhana*.
Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta entered the meditative absorption that had just been described by the Blessed One.

As soon as Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta had entered that absorption, this trichiliocosm— equal in extent to a trichiliocosm composed of atoms from hundreds of thousands of myriad world-systems— [became manifest].
Having caused the earth to tremble and having illuminated it with a great radiance, he displayed his own empowerment of purity and spoke these mantra-words:
"Homage to all Buddhas!"

Homage to those who have emerged from the intrinsic nature of non-existence; homage to the Pratyekabuddhas and the noble Śrāvakas; homage to the Bodhisattvas, the lords established on the ten stages, the Bodhisattvas, the Mahāsattvas.
Namely: *uṃ*!
*khakha khāhi khāhi*, O subduer of wicked beings!

You who hold a sword, a mace, an axe, and a noose in your hands; four-armed, four-faced, six-legged! Go, go, O destroyer of great obstacles! You of deformed countenance, O terrifier of all spirits, you who utter a loud laugh, you who are clothed in a tiger skin!
Perform, perform all rites!
Cut, cut all mantras! Pierce, pierce the supreme mudrā!
Draw forth, draw forth all mudrās!
Grind down, grind down all the wicked!
Enter, enter into the center of the maṇḍala!
O ender of the son of Vivasvat, accomplish, accomplish my purpose!
Burn, burn! Cook, cook! Do not delay, do not delay! Remember your vow! Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ! Shatter, shatter! O fulfiller of all hopes! O Blessed One, why do you tarry? Accomplish all my aims! Svāhā!
This great wrathful king of the Blessed Mañjuśrī, named Yamāntaka, slays even King Yama; he brings him under his power— how much more so any other sentient being?
As soon as the Great Wrathful King had been spoken, all sentient beings approached the presence of the Blessed One— afflicted, terrified, trembling, agitated in mind, and broken-hearted;
they had no other refuge and no other protection.

There is no other refuge, except for the Buddha, the Blessed One, and Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta. Now, whatever beings there may be— those moving on land, those moving in water, those moving through the air, whether stationary or mobile, born from a womb, born from an egg, born from moisture, or born spontaneously— all who are reckoned among sentient beings;

They too, stationed in infinite and boundless world-systems— whether above, below, across, or in the cardinal and intermediate directions— were instantly driven away by that Great Wrathful King himself and brought here;
and this is the Wrathful King.

It should not be recited in the presence of one who is not free from passion, for he too might die or wither away. Having empowered oneself according to the *samaya*, it should be recited before an image of the Buddha, or before an image of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta.
It should not be recited anywhere for the sake of any other ritual purpose;
the reason is that such a cause would lead to great calamity, great ruin, and self-destruction.
For the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, and the Bodhisattvas, the Mahāsattvas, are supremely compassionate, and they possess only the wisdom of omniscience.

He who establishes [beings] in the state of peace, who brings the entire realm of sentient beings to the attainment of nirvāṇa, whose teaching is desired, who is joined with the three measures, who illuminates the practice of mantras so as not to sever the lineage of the Three Jewels, who— with a mind that is the natural outflow of the power of great compassion—
overcomes the forces of Māra, destroys great obstacles, wards off wicked kings, and overcomes the power of the self.

He spoke with a mind free from all conceptualization and discursive thought, having attained great loving-kindness, great compassion, great equanimity, and great sympathetic joy; he spoke for the sake of warding off hostile forces, paralyzing them, causing them to fall, destroying them, subduing them, drying them up, and pleasing them; for the purpose of revealing the practice of his own mantra, and for the swift accomplishment of tasks through the increase of longevity, health, and sovereignty.

Then those nāgas and great nāgas, yakṣas and great yakṣas, rākṣasas and great rākṣasas, piśācas and great piśācas, pūtanās and great pūtanās, kaṭapūtanās and great kaṭapūtanās, mārutas and great mārutas, kūṣmāṇḍas and great kūṣmāṇḍas,
vyāḍas and great vyāḍas, vetāḍas and great vetāḍas, kambojas and great kambojas, bhaginīs and great bhaginīs, and ḍākinīs and great ḍākinīs—

The Cūṣakas and Mahācūṣakas, the Utsārakas and Mahotsārakas, the Ḍimphikas and Mahāḍimphikas, the Kimpakas and Mahākimpakas, the Rogas and Mahārogas, the Apasmāras and Mahāpasmāras, the Grahas and Mahāgrahas, the Ākāśamātṛs and Mahākāśamātṛs, the Rūpiṇīs and Mahārūpiṇīs,
the Krandanas and Mahākrandanās, the Chāyās and Mahācchāyās, and the Preṣakas and Mahāpreṣakas.

Kiṅkaras and Mahākiṅkaras, Yakṣiṇīs and Mahāyakṣiṇīs, Piśācīs and Mahāpiśācīs, fevers and Mahāfevers, quartan fevers and Mahāquartan fevers, constant fevers, irregular fevers, continuous fevers, momentary fevers, those caused by wind, bile, phlegm, or a combination of all three; vidyās and Mahāvidyās, Siddhas and Mahāsiddhas.

Yogins and great yogins, sages and great sages; kiṅkaras and great kiṅkaras, mahoragas and great mahoragas; gandharvas and great gandharvas, gods and great gods, humans and great humans; provinces and great provinces, oceans and great oceans, rivers and great rivers, mountains and great mountains, treasures and great treasures, of the earth and the great earth.

Trees and great trees, female birds and great female birds; kings, great kings, Śakras, Mahendras, Vāsavas, Kratus, and Bhūtas in the sky; Īśāna, Yama, Brahmā, Mahābrahmā, Vaivasvata, Dhanada, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Virūpākṣa, Kubera, Pūrṇabhadra, Pañcika, Jambhala, Sambhala, Kūṣmala, Hārīti, Harikeśa, and Harihārīti.
Piṅgalā, Priyaṅkara, Arthaṅkara, Jālandhara, Lokendra, Upendra, Guhyaka, Mahāguhyaka, Cala, Capala, Jalacara, Sātata, Giri, Hemagiri, Mahāgiri, Kūtākṣa, and Triśiras—
along with these and other great yakṣa generals, surrounded by retinues of many hundreds of thousands of millions of yakṣas, were right there.
In the great assembly circle within the palace of the Pure Abodes, we gathered and sat down through the empowerment of the Bodhisattvas and the application of their miraculous power,
in order to hear the Dharma.
Also those great rākṣasa kings, accompanied by retinues of many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of rākṣasas, were brought forth by the Great Wrathful King;
namely: Rāvaṇa, Praviṇa, Vidrāvaṇa, Śaṅkukarṇa, Kumbha, Kumbhakarṇa, Samantakarṇa, and Yama.
Vibhīṣaṇa, Ghora, Sughora, Yakṣa, Yamaghaṇṭa, Indrajit, Lokajit, Yodhana, Suyodhana, Śūla, Triśūla, Triśiras, and Anantaśiras— all these assembled together to listen to the Dharma.
Also those great piśācas with retinues of many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions—
as namely Pīlu, Upapīlu, Supīlu, Anantapīlu, Manoratha, Amanoratha, Sutāya, Grasana, Sudhāma, Ghora, and Ghorarūpī— gathered together to hear the Dharma; as did those great nāga kings.

Accompanied by retinues of many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of *nāgas*, they were brought forth by the Wrathful King and through the empowerment of the Bodhisattva’s supernatural power.
They were as follows: Nanda, Upananda, Kambala, Upakambala, Vāsuki, Ananta, Takṣaka, Padma, and Mahāpadma.

Saṅkhapāla, Saṅkha, Saṅkhapāla, Karkoṭaka, Kulika, Akulika, Māṇa, Kalaśoda, Kuliśika, Cāṃpeya, Maṇināga, Mānabhañja, Dukura, Upadukura, Lakuṭa, Mahālakuṭa, Śveta, Śvetabhadra, Nīla, Nīlāmbuda, Kṣīroda, Apalāla, Sāgara, and Upasāgara.

Together with these and other great nāga kings, surrounded by retinues of many hundreds of thousands of great nāgas, they assembled and sat down in that great circle of the assembly to hear the Dharma.
And those sages and great sages as well—
namely: Ātreya, Vasiṣṭha, Gautama, Bhagīratha, Jahnu, Aṅgiras, Agasti, Pulasti,
Vyāsa, Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa-Gautama, Agni, Aṅgirasa, Jāmadagnya, Āstīka, Muni, Munivara, Aśvara, and Vaiśampāyana.

Parāśara, Paraśu, Yogeśvara, Pippala, Pippalāda, Vālmīka, and Mārkaṇḍeya— these and other great ṛṣis, accompanied by retinues of many hundreds of thousands of great ṛṣis, approached that assembly circle. Having paid homage to the Blessed One Śākyamuni, they sat down to listen to and rejoice in the Bodhisattvapiṭaka concerning the purpose of mantra practice.
Those great kings of the mahoragas also entered that circle of the assembly and sat down;
namely, Bheruṇḍa, Bhūrūṇḍa, Maruṇḍa, Mārīca, Dīpa, and Pradīpa.
Those who were the kings of the *garuḍas* also assembled in that circle of the assembly, with retinues of many hundreds of thousands.
They were as follows: Suparṇa, Śvetaparṇa, Pannaga, Parṇaya, Sujātapakṣa, Ajātapakṣa, Manojava, Pannaganāśana, Vainateya, Vainateya, Bharadvāja, Śakuna, and Mahāśakuna.
And the kings of birds—
these too would assemble in that circle of the assembly.
Those kings of the *kinnaras* as well, accompanied by retinues of many hundreds of thousands of *kinnaras*, also assembled in that circle of the assembly.

They were as follows: Druma, Upadruma, Sudruma, Anantadruma, Lokadruma, Ledruma, Ghanoraska, Mahoraska, Mahojaska, Mahoja, Maharddhika, Viruta, Susvara, Manojña, Cittonmādakara, Unnata, Upekṣaka, Karuṇa, and Aruṇa.
These and other great kings of the kinnaras, accompanied by retinues of many hundreds of thousands of kinnaras, assembled there to hear the Dharma.
Likewise, there are Brahmā Sahāmpati, Mahābrahmā, Ābhāsvara, Prabhāsvara, Śuddhābha, Puṇyābha, Aṭṭaha, Atapā, Akaniṣṭhā, Sukaniṣṭhā, Lokaniṣṭhā, Ākiñcanyā, Naivakiñcanyā, Ākāśānantyā,
Naivākāśānantyā, Sudṛśā, Sudarśanā, Sunirmitā, Paranirmitā, the Śuddhāvāsa deities, the Tuṣita deities, the Yāma deities, the Trāyastriṃśa deities, and the Cāturmahārājika deities.
The Sadāmattas, Mālādhāras, Karoṭapāṇis, Vīṇātṛtīyakas, those dwelling on mountains, those dwelling on peaks, those dwelling on summits,

those dwelling in Alakā, those dwelling in cities, those dwelling in celestial palaces, those moving through the atmosphere, those dwelling on the earth, those dwelling in trees, and those dwelling in houses; likewise the lords of the Dānavas— headed by Prahlāda, Bali, Rāhu, Vemacitti, Sucitti, Kṣemacitti, Devacitti, and Bāhu Rāhu— accompanied by retinues of many hundreds of thousands of millions of Dānavas, possessing diverse modes of movement.
The Asuras, who fight with the gods for various reasons,
would also assemble in that circle of the assembly to behold,
worship, and attend upon the miraculous manifestation of the Bodhisattvas through the Buddha’s empowerment.
And those planets and great planets who act for the benefit of the world, moving through the intermediate space—
namely: Āditya, Soma, Aṅgāraka, Budha, Bṛhaspati, Śukra, Śanaiścara, Rāhu, Kampa, Ketu, Aśani, Nirghāta, Tāra, Dhvaja, Ghora, Dhūmra, Vajra, Ṛkṣa, Vṛṣṭi, Upavṛṣṭi, Naṣṭārka, Nirnaṣṭa, and Haśānta.
Mārṣṭi, Ṛṣṭi, Tuṣṭi, Lokānta, Kṣaya, Vinipāta, Āpāta, Tarka, Mastaka, Yugānta, Śmaśāna, Piśita, Raudra, Śveta, Abhija, Abhijata, Maitra, Śaṅku, Triśaṅku, Lūtha, Raudraka, Kratunāśana, Balavān,
Ghora, Aruṇa, Vihasita, Mārṣṭi, Skanda, Sanat, Upasanat, Kumārakrīḍana, Hasana, and Prahasana.

Nartapaka, Nartaka, Khaja, and Virūpa— these great grahas, surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of followers, gathered and sat down in that Śuddhāvāsa palace through the Buddha’s empowerment. Furthermore, those constellations that move through the sky, accompanied by retinues of many hundreds of thousands of constellations, [also gathered there].
Namely: Aśvinī, Bharaṇī, Kṛttikā, Rohiṇī, Mṛgaśirā, Ārdrā, Punarvasū, Puṣya, Āśleṣā, Maghā, both Phalgunīs, Hastā, Citrā, Svāti, Viśākhā, Anurādhā, Jyeṣṭhā, Mūlā, both Āṣāḍhas, Śravaṇā, Dhaniṣṭhā,
Śatabhiṣā, both Bhadrapadas, Revatī, Devatī, Prabhijā, Punarṇavā, Jyoti, and Aṅgirasā.
Nakṣatrikā, both Phalgu and Phalguvatī, Lokapravarā, Pravarāṇikā, Śreyasī, Lokamātā, Īrā, Ūhā, Vahā, Arthavatī, and Asārthā—

these are the queens of the constellations who, surrounded by a retinue of many hundreds of thousands of constellations, gathered in that palace of the Śuddhāvāsa deities within that great assembly circle through the empowerment of the Buddha.
I sat down together with them.
There are thirty-six signs (*rāśi*), namely: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius,
Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces, Monkey, Lesser Jar, Rhinoceros, Sword, Elephant, Buffalo, Deity, and Human.

O Victorious over the worlds of birds, gandharvas, and sentient beings; O You of fierce splendor, moonlight, shadow, earth, darkness, passion, secondary passion, suffering, happiness, liberation, awakening, solitary realizers, disciples, hell-beings, vidyādharas, great brilliance, great majesty, animals, pretas, asuras, flesh-eaters, piśācas, yakṣas, rākṣasas; O You who pervade all stages, the elemental spirits, the downward-flowing, the upward-moving, the horizontal, and the blossomed!
The meditators established in yoga are of three types: superior, middling, and inferior.
These constitute the great multitudes, surrounded by hundreds of thousands of various multitudes, [proceeding] toward the abode of the Śuddhāvāsa heaven.
They approached the circle of the great assembly;
having approached, they prostrated at the feet of the Blessed One and sat down in their respective places.
There were also those great yakṣiṇīs,
surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of yakṣiṇīs,
such as: Sulocanā, Subhrū, Sukeśā, Susvarā, Sumatī, Vasumatī, Citrākṣī, Pūrāṃśā, and Guhyakā.
Suguhyakā, Mekhalā, Sumekhalā, Padmoccā, Abhayā, Jayā, Vijayā, Revatikā, Keśinī, Keśāntā, Anilā, Manoharā, Manovatī, Kusumāvatī, Kusumapuravāsinī, Piṅgalā, Hārītī, Vīramatī, Vīrā, Suvīrā,
Sughorā, Ghoravatī, Surasundarī, Surasā, Guhyottamārī, Vatavāsinī, Aśokā, and Andhārasundarī.

Ālokasundarī, Prabhāvatī, Atiśayavatī, Rūpavatī, Surūpā, Asitā, Saumyā, Kāṇā, Menā, Nandinī, Upanandinī, and Lokāntarā— these great yakṣiṇīs, accompanied by retinues of many hundreds of thousands of yakṣiṇīs, stood at a distance from that great assembly circle, bowing in homage to the Blessed One Śākyamuni.
Those great piśācīs as well,
surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of piśācīs, also gathered there, paying homage to the Blessed One Śākyamuni.

They were as follows: Maṇḍitikā, Pāṃsupiśācī, Ulkāpiśācī, Jvālāpiśācī, Bhasmodgirā, Piśitāśinī, Durdharā, Bhrāmarī, Mohanī, Tarjanī, Rohiṇikā, Govāhiṇikā, Lokāntikā, Bhasmāntikā, Pīluvatī, Bahulavatī, Bahulā, Durdāntā, Dhaṇā, Cihnitikā, Dhūmāntikā, Dhūmā, and Sudhūmā.
These great piśācīs, surrounded by retinues of many hundreds of thousands of piśācīs,
also entered that maṇḍala of the great assembly.
And those Mothers and Great Mothers who roam the world,
who cause harm to sentient beings and receive offerings of oblations and garlands—
namely: Brahmāṇī, Māheśvarī, Vaiṣṇavī, Kaumārī, Cāmuṇḍā, Vārāhī, Aindrī, Yāmyā, and Āgneyā.
Vaivasvatī, Lokāntakarī, Vāruṇī, Aiśānī, Vāyavyā, Paraprāṇaharā, Sukhamaṇḍitikā, Śakunī, Mahāśakunī, Pūtanā, Kaṭapūtanā, and Skandā—
these are the Great Mothers, each with a retinue of many hundreds of thousands of mothers.
They too remained there, uttering the words "Homage to the Buddha! toward that great circle of the assembly.
In this way, hundreds of thousands of humans— both sentient and non-sentient beings— from the great Avīci hell up to the summit of existence,
the entire expanse of space in the interval between them became completely filled.
Within the assembly of beings, there was no hostility toward any living creature whatsoever.
And through the Buddha’s empowerment and the adornment of the Bodhisattva Saṅgha, all beings beheld the Blessed Buddha and Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta standing before them at their very heads.
Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni, having surveyed the entire world-system with his Buddha-eye, addressed Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta:

"Speak, speak, O pure being! Recite the Bodhisattvapiṭaka, which is the detailed exposition of the chapter on the samādhi for the definitive determination of the meaning of mantra practice, whenever you deem it to be the right time."
Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, having been granted permission by the Blessed One Śākyamuni, entered the meditative absorption named *Gaganasvabhāvavyūhālaṅkāra-vajrasaṃhatakaṭhinasantānavyūhālaṅkāra*.

As soon as Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta had entered that absorption, he empowered that abode of the Pure Abodes (*śuddhāvāsabhavana*), which extended for many hundreds of thousands of yojanas, so that it became composed of vajra.
Therein, those many yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, maruts, and piśācas— in short, the entire realm of sentient beings— by means of the bodhisattva’s empowerment,

became established and seated within that palace which resembled a diamond-jewel, remaining without harming one another. Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, perceiving that great assembly gathered there, addressed Yamāntaka, the King of Wrath.
O, O Great King of Wrath, destroyer of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas! Protect, protect this great assembly-circle and all sentient beings; bring them under your control!
Subdue the wicked!
Awaken the gentle!
Purify her who is unpurified.
Until I have spoken the Bodhisattva-piṭaka concerning the practice of my own mantras— the extensive ritual procedures for the maṇḍala of mantra practice— go outside and protect her.
Thus addressed, the Great Wrathful King, assuming a most hideous form, went forth to protect all beings and to uphold the teaching.

Surrounded by hundreds of thousands of various wrathful deities, Yamāntaka, the King of Wrath, stood encircling the entire assembly circle on all sides— in the four directions, above, below, and across— emitting a terrible roar.

Then they all became gentle and well-disposed, and they did not transgress his command. And they heard this proclamation: "Whosoever should transgress this agreement, his head shall split open like the cluster of flowers on an *ajaka* plant."
And that is the empowerment of the bodhisattva.
Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta spoke these words on the dharma-steps for the purpose of his own mantra practice:
"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is endowed with even a single dharma, his mantras will attain accomplishment. Which is that one?"
That is to say, by perceiving all phenomena as being free from conceptual proliferation (*niṣprapañca*).
For a bodhisattva established in two qualities, mantras shall attain accomplishment.
Which two?

Not abandoning the thought of awakening (*bodhicitta*) and equanimity toward all sentient beings—through these two dharmas, they attain the fulfillment of the instruction on the purpose of their own mantra practice. Which two? Through these two.
Not abandoning any sentient being by means of guarding the vows of the bodhisattva’s ethical discipline, and not abandoning one’s own mantra—
when a bodhisattva who has first produced the thought of awakening is endowed with these four qualities, his mantras will attain accomplishment.
What are the four?

Not abandoning one’s own mantra, not interrupting the practice of others’ mantras, extending loving-kindness toward all sentient beings, and having a mind cultivated by great compassion— through these four qualities, the mantras of a bodhisattva who has first generated the thought of awakening shall attain accomplishment.
Those dharmas which constitute the convergence of the Bodhisattva-piṭaka and the actualization of mantra-practice shall lead to the fulfillment of awakening.
Which five?
Dwelling in secluded places and not being hostile toward other beings.
Not looking toward worldly mantras,
and establishing oneself in ethical discipline, learning, and right conduct— these five qualities lead to the fulfillment of the purpose of mantra practice.
Six qualities lead to the fulfillment of the purpose of mantra practice.
What are the six? They are:
the non-interruption of faith in the Three Jewels;
the non-interruption of faith in the bodhisattvas,
the non-censure of mundane and supramundane mantras,
and the honoring of the non-proliferated realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).
Not rejecting the Mahāyāna sūtras whose meanings are profound; having a mind free from weariness; seeking the practice of mantras; and not falling away from the side of wholesome qualities.
These six factors lead to the convergence of the accomplishment of the mantra practice of knowledge (*vidyācaryā*).
Seven factors lead to the entry into the mantra practice suitable for the time of accomplishing knowledge.
What are the seven?
It is the profound method;

it is the liberation of the bodhisattva practice through the cultivation, recitation, teaching, study, and transcription of the *Prajñāpāramitā*; it is the entry into the method of the Mahāyāna Dharma and the equipment of a bodhisattva by means of observing the rules of time and place, and through the practice of recitation, fire-offerings (*homa*), silence, and austerity, which result in unimpeded movement, intelligence, mindfulness, wisdom, and fortitude; and it is skill in the performance of the rites for one's own mantras, including their invocation, protection, and accomplishment.

Great compassion, great loving-kindness, great equanimity, and great sympathetic joy— due to the realization of the non-existence of the perfections, due to the convergence in suchness of the realm of sentient beings and the realm of phenomena which is free from conceptual proliferation, due to the thorough seeking of the omniscient gnosis in its two aspects, and due to the lack of longing for the Lesser Vehicle, there is no abandonment of any sentient being. These seven qualities bring the accomplishment of the mantra of knowledge and ignorance to full completion.

What are these [factors]? They are: faith in the results of what has not been seen and what has been seen; curiosity and the desire for knowledge; and the absence of malice. These lead to the attainment of the eight dharmas, the accomplishment of the purpose of the mantras, and their convergence. This occurs through the manifestation of purity resulting from the Bodhisattva’s grace; through the unerring reception of mantras and reverence for the Guru;
and through receiving the instructions of the Ācārya regarding the mantras and tantras of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, remaining free from contradiction, and relinquishing all one's possessions.

By means of demonstrating skill in perceiving dreams regarding the presence or absence of sites for the accomplishment of spiritual powers (*siddhakṣetra*); by being free from the stain of stinginess and having entirely cast off sloth and torpor while initiating vigor through the constant offering of oneself to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; in brief, by being girded with the great armor of insatiable roots of virtue; by desiring to strike down all obstacles; by possessing a physical form of great renown that aspires to the great enjoyments of approaching the seat of awakening (*bodhimaṇḍa*);
and by meeting with the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, a spiritual friend who is never separated from association with persons of great renown.
These eight factors lead to the attainment of the goal and the fulfillment of the practice of mantras.
In brief, friends, for one who is not devoid of the thought of awakening (*bodhicitta*), who has not abandoned the Three Jewels, and who— though even of extremely immoral conduct—

is tireless in mind and constantly devoted, my extensive array of mantra chapters, which arises from a mind overflowing with the result of the infinite and marvelous conduct of a bodhisattva, shall be accomplished.
One must not proceed otherwise;
having become free from conceptual construction, it should be accomplished even for the sake of mere inquiry.
Then that entire assembly—empowered by the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, and noble Śrāvakas—uttered these words:

"Excellent, excellent, O Son of the Conqueror! This teaching of the Dharma, which follows the entry into the method of the Dharma for the performance of the purpose of the various mantra-practices, has been well-expounded for the benefit of all sentient beings. Oh, Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta! This eloquent discourse, which conforms to the teaching of the diverse Dharmas and accords with the practice of mantras, is truly sublime."
For whoever, O Great King, shall recite, uphold, and attend to this chapter on the assembly,
Or, having placed him at the forefront in battle upon an elephant, he will station him there;
or he will worship him with various flowers, incense, perfumes, and ointments;
and we shall bring his adversaries and enemies under his control.
"We shall bring about the defeat of the enemy's army.
Or, having had it written in a book, one will keep it in one's own home;
for that son of good family or daughter of good family, or for the great king or queen, or for the monk or nun—
For a layman or a laywoman,
there shall be great protection, great wealth,
and long life.
"I shall bring about long life, health, and the constant increase of enjoyments."
When this had been said, that entire assembly became silent.

From the *Mahākalpa* that sets forth the practice of the mantras of the Mahāyāna, from the extensive section on the miraculous manifestations of the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, this is the first chapter, the Chapter on the Assembly, from the *Mūlakalpa*.
(Vaidya 17) Now begins the second chapter:
(The Chapter on the Ritual for the Mandala).
Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, having surveyed the entire circle of the assembly, entered the samādhi called "The Survey that Penetrates the Nature of All Beings.
As soon as Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta had entered it, a ray of light issued forth from the region of his navel.

Accompanied by a retinue of many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of rays, it illuminated the entire realm of sentient beings in every direction, and then, having illuminated that very abode of the Śuddhāvāsa gods, it remained there.

Then indeed, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi addressed Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta: "Speak, speak, O Son of the Jina! [Speak] the *dhāraṇī* named 'Entry into the Samaya of All Beings,' by entering which one enters your entire collection of mantras, both mundane and supramundane."
And they attain the accomplishment of mantras.
When the Lord of the Guhyakas, the King of Yakṣas, had spoken thus, Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta proclaimed the *Paramaguhyamaṇḍalatantra*,
which effects the manifestation of the rite named "The Incitement of All Vidyās."
Raising his right hand, he beckoned to the circle of the assembly with the tip of his finger.
From that fingertip, many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of vidyārājas issued forth;
having issued forth, they illuminated the entire realm of the Śuddhāvāsa deities with a great radiance and remained there.

Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta [expounded] the heart-mantra of Yamāntaka, the King of Wrath, which accomplishes all rites; it is the Sole Hero, effective for summoning and dismissal, pacification, enrichment, and malevolent magic;

it grants invisibility, travel through the sky, entry into the subterranean realm (pātāla), movement upon trees, attraction, causing enmity, and subjugation; and it provides the offering of all perfumes, garlands, ointments, and lamps within one's own mantra-tantras.
In brief, however one practices, so is the Great King of Wrath—the imperishable one named Mahāvīrya, the accomplisher of all aims—being accomplished.
And what is that? Oṃ Āḥ.
Hrūṃ! This is the heart-mantra of the Great Wrathful One;
it is effective for all rites, taught by the Great Being Mañjughoṣa for all maṇḍalas and all mantra practices, and it destroys all obstacles.
Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, raising his right hand, placed it upon the head of the Wrathful One and spoke thus: "Homage to you, the Buddhas of all [times]. May the Blessed Buddhas attend to me."
"Whatever Bodhisattvas of great supernatural power, infinite and boundless, are established in the world-systems of the ten directions, may they empower this samaya!
Having spoken thus, he whirled that King of Wrath and hurled him.

Immediately upon being hurled, the Great King of Wrath, in a single moment, subdued and brought under control all those beings of evil intent throughout the entire world-system, even those of great supernatural power.
He caused that great assembly circle to enter the abode of the Śuddhāvāsa gods;
having established them in their proper positions, he became surrounded by a garland of flames on all sides and stood upon the heads of the wicked beings.

Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, having again surveyed that circle of the assembly, said: "Listen, all you beings! For this King of Wrath will bring about the subjugation of anyone who should transgress this my *samaya*.

Since the paths of words concerning the meaning of the secret mantras of the *samaya* of the Blessed Buddhas and the Bodhisattvas of great supernatural power are not to be transgressed, I shall speak of them by way of a concise exposition."
Listen to this and attend to it well and thoroughly; I shall speak.
Homage to all Buddhas!
Oṃ ra ra smara, you who possess the form of a youth with unimpeded command, hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā!
"O Noble Ones, this is my root mantra.
The mudrā known as the Great Five-Peaked Mudrā belongs to the noble Mañjuśrī; one should employ it with this root mantra, for it becomes a heart-mantra effective for all rites.
It is the auspicious Buddha who performs all actions."
Oṃ dhānyada namaḥ.
And here there is a mudrā known as the "Three-Pointed," which increases all enjoyments.
And here there is also a near-heart mantra (upahṛdaya).
Externally, there is *hūṃ*.
And here the mudrā is known as the "Three-Pointed," which attracts all sentient beings.
Furthermore, the supreme heart-mantra (*paramahṛdaya*) is as follows:
Muṃ. And here the mudrā is known as the Peacock Throne (mayūrāsana), which brings all sentient beings under control;
it is the heart of all Buddhas.

Furthermore, there is another eight-syllable mantra named Mahāvīra, which is the supreme excellence, a great purifier, the severer of the path of the three realms of existence, the preventer of all miserable rebirths, the bringer of all peace, the performer of all rites, secure, and that which leads to the attainment of Nirvana— standing before one like the Buddha himself in person.

Mañjuśrī himself, this Bodhisattva, for the sake of all sentient beings, has appeared in the form of a mantra as a supreme heart-essence that fulfills all hopes; by the mere recollection of which one purifies even the five deeds of immediate retribution— how much more so, then, [the purification of] other [sins]?
And what is that?
Om āḥ dhīra hūṃ khacaraḥ.
This, O worthy ones, is I myself—the eight-syllable Great Hero, the supreme secret heart-mantra, which stands as a condition for Buddhahood itself.
In brief, he is skilled in all tasks and brings them to ultimate completion; this is the great *guṇa*. And here the mudrā is known as Mahāvīrā, which fulfills all hopes.
The mantra for invocation is as follows:
Oṃ he he! To you whose own form is that of a youth, who awakens all the speech of children, come, Blessed One, come!
You who hold a lotus from the play of a youth, stay, stay in the center of the maṇḍala! Remember your pledge!
O you of unimpeded command, hūṃ!
Do not delay!
Ru ru phaṭ svāhā!
"O Blessed One, this is the invocation mantra of Mañjuśrī for all sentient beings,
all bodhisattvas, all pratyekabuddhas, noble śrāvakas, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, piśācas, rākṣasas, and all spirits.
Having consecrated sandalwood water seven times with this, one should scatter it in the four directions— above, below, across, and everywhere."
May all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, Mañjuśrī himself with his retinue, all worldly and transcendent mantras, all hosts of spirits, and all sentient beings come.
Homage to all Buddhas whose teachings are unimpeded!
Oṃ dhura dhura dhura dhūpavāsini dhūpārciṣi hūṃ tiṣṭha samayamanusmara svāhā!
The incense mantra:
Having combined sandalwood, camphor, and saffron, one should then offer incense.
Thus, the minds of the Tathāgatas and all the Bodhisattvas who have arrived are nourished by the incense, and they become attracted.
And there is a mudrā here, renowned as the *mālā*, which is auspicious and attracts all sentient beings.
This very same mudrā, the auspicious *padmamālā*, is also for the mantra of invocation.
And when all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have arrived, as well as all sentient beings who have arrived, the *arghya* offering should be presented.

Having stirred water with camphor, sandalwood, and saffron, and having mixed it with one or another of these flowers—*jātī*, *navamālikā*, *vārṣika*, *punnāga*, *nāga*, *vakula*, and *piṇḍitagara*—or with any fragrant flower appropriate to the season, the *arghya* offering should be presented with this mantra:
"Homage to all Buddhas whose teaching is unimpeded! It is as follows: *He he mahākāruṇika viśvarūpadhāriṇi*!"
Accept the *arghya*, cause it to be accepted; remember the pledge (*samaya*); stay, stay! Enter into the center of the maṇḍala, enter! O you who have compassion for all beings, take, take! HŪṂ!
To the one who wanders through the sky, svāhā!
And here the mudrā is renowned as Pūrṇā, which follows all the Buddhas;
it is constant. And here the fragrance mantra is as follows:
Homage to all Buddhas! Homage to the Tathāgata Samantagandhāvabhāsaśrī!
It is as follows: *Gandhe gandhe gandhāḍhye gandhamanorame pratīccha pratīccheyaṃ gandhaṃ samatānusāriṇe svāhā!* Furthermore, there is here a mudrā called Pallavā, which fulfills all aspirations.
And here is the mantra for the flowers:
"Homage to all Buddhas whose teachings are unimpeded!
Homage to the Tathāgata Saṅkusumitarāja!"
Namely: *kusume kusume kusumāḍhye kusumapuravāsini kusumāvati svāhā*.
With that very incense mantra and with the same incense previously mentioned, one should fumigate.
Having paid homage to all the Buddhas, whose forms are inconceivable and marvelous,
I shall proclaim the *bali* mantra spoken by the Perfectly Enlightened One.

Homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas whose teachings are unimpeded. It is as follows: *He he, Blessed One, Great Being, looked upon by the Buddhas! Do not delay! Accept this offering! Grasp it! Hūṃ hūṃ, O All-Universal One! Ra ra ṭa ṭa phaṭ svāhā!* And with this, one should cause the offering to be presented.
And there is the offering for all spirits (*sarvabhautika*).
In this regard, there is a mudrā called Śakti, which wards off all malevolent beings.
Homage to all Buddhas whose teachings are unimpeded and who destroy all blinding darkness! Homage to the Tathāgata Samantajyotigandhāvabhāsaśrī!

It is as follows: "He he! O Blessed One, whose body is adorned with hundreds of thousands of light-rays! Manifest, manifest! O you whose form is illuminated by the universal flames of the great bodhisattvas! Leap, leap! Behold, behold all sentient beings! Svāhā! This is the lamp mantra.
And with this, one should cause a lamp to be offered.
The mudrā is named Vikāsinī, the beholder of all sentient beings. Homage to all Buddhas whose teachings are unimpeded!
Namely: *jvala jvala jvālaya jvālaya / hūṃ / vivodhaka harikṛṣṇapiṅgala svāhā*.
These are the fire-offering mantras.
And here there is a mudrā known as the "Casket" (sampuṭa), renowned throughout the world;
it was previously taught by the best of sages for the sake of the wise Bodhisattva, illuminating all sentient beings.
Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi:
"O Lord of the Guhyakas, these mantra-words, together with their secrets and supreme mysteries, belong to your renowned family; they are formidable and always fierce."
This indeed is [the essence] of all mantras being accomplished by the wise.
This vidyā shall now be proclaimed for the purpose of utterly destroying him who is renowned as Mūrdhūṭaka, [the one] belonging to both the Kātyāyana and Gautama lineages. Mmk_2.3 //
Homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas whose teachings are unimpeded! Oṃ! Act! Act! Perform! Perform my task! Shatter! Shatter all obstacles!
Even more so, [subdue] all Vajra-Vināyakas!
O you who bring an end to life at the crown of the head, you of great and hideous form! Cook, cook all the wicked!
O you who bring an end to the life of Mahāgaṇapati! Bind, bind all the seizing spirits (grahas)!
O six-faced one, six-armed one, six-legged one, bring Rudra!
Bring Viṣṇu!
Bring the gods beginning with Brahmā!
Do not delay, do not delay! Flash, flash! Cause [him] to enter into the center of the maṇḍala! Remember the pledge!
HŪṂ HŪṂ HŪṂ HŪṂ HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ.
O Lord of the Supreme Guhyakas, this is that supreme secret, the Great Hero Mañjuśrī, the great wrathful king named Ṣaṇmukha, the destroyer of all obstacles.
Merely by reciting this, the bodhisattvas established on the ten stages flee in terror.
How much more so, then, evil obstructors!
By the mere recitation of this, great protection is established.
And here there is a mudrā known as the "Great Spear" (Mahāśūlā), which destroys all obstacles.
This is the heart-mantra of this very King of Wrath:
Oṃ hrīḥṃ jñīḥ vikṛtānana hūṃ!
Destroy all enemies, paralyze them! Phaṭ phaṭ svāhā!
By means of this mantra, one causes all enemies to be seized by a great piercing pain (mahāśūlaroga) or by a quartan fever;
or, by reciting it a hundred times, until they submit or do not attain a state of friendliness.

If, however, one develops a compassionate mind, there will be no liberation at the end of the recitation; he will die. This [rite] is to be performed for those who have harmed the Triple Gem, not for those with gentle minds; in such cases, the Mahāśūla mudrā alone should be employed.
And here there is an *upahṛdaya* (near-heart mantra):
*oṃ hrīḥṃ kālarūpa huṃ khaṃ svāhā*. The *mudrā* to be employed is that of the Great Trident itself.
This supreme heart-mantra causes all malevolent beings to do whatever one desires.
The single-syllable mantra empowered by all the Buddhas is "HŪṂ.
This performs all activities.
The mudrā should be employed with the Great Spear alone;
it wards off all misfortunes and,
in brief, brings all spirits under control.
This King of Wrath is to be employed in all rites; recitation within the mandala at the time of accomplishment is especially distinguished.
The mantras for dismissal are as follows:
*Namaḥ sarvabuddhānām apratihataśāsanānām*.
Namely: Victory! Victory! Well-victorious one! O you of great compassion, you who possess all forms! Go, go to your own abode, and dismiss all the Buddhas;
cause them, together with their retinues, to enter their own abodes. Remember the pledge!
"May all my purposes be accomplished; fulfill my heart's desire, svāhā!
This is the dismissal mantra (*visarjanamantra*), which should be employed in all rites.
The mudrā is renowned as the *bhadrapīṭha*.
One should also cause him to offer a seat;
by mentally reciting [the mantra] seven times, there is dismissal from all mundane and supramundane mandalas and from the mantras themselves, and the accomplishment of the mantras occurs.
This should be employed during the observances of the pledges, the recitations, and the fixed times.

Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, having again gazed upon that palace of the Śuddhāvāsa deities, spoke once more to that great circle of the assembly and to his own host of knowledge-mantras and ritual sections:
"Homage to all the Buddhas whose teachings are unimpeded!"
Oṃ riṭi svāhā!
This is the vidyā-mantra named Keśinī, a follower of Mañjuśrī, which performs all rites.
It is to be employed with the great five-crested mudrā in all rituals for neutralizing poisons.
Homage to all Buddhas whose teachings are unimpeded!
Oṃ niṭi!
This is the vidyā named Upakeśinī, effective for all rites; one should employ it together with the Vikāsinī mudrā.
In all rites concerning the grahas:
Homage to all Buddhas of unimpeded movement! Oṃ niḥ!
This vidyā, named Balinī, is auspicious and performs all activities.
When joined with the Bhadrapīṭha mudrā, she brings the yakṣiṇī certainly under control.
Homage to all the Buddhas, who possess inconceivable and wondrous forms;
joined with the seal and the power, she is the destroyer of all ḍākinīs.
Oṃ jñaiḥ svāhā!
This knowledge-mantra named Kāpatalinī was spoken by Mañjughoṣa;
it is praised by all the Buddhas everywhere and possesses a divine form.
Homage to all Buddhas who move with unimpeded gait!
It is as follows: *Oṃ varade svāhā*.
One who seeks excellence should employ this very three-crested mudrā.
The goddess, assuming many forms, swiftly accomplishes the attainment of enjoyments.
