This second field of Śaniścara was declared of old;
it is designated as the sign of Capricorn and is the dispeller of all misfortunes.
If a wise knower of mantras, staying there, should undertake ritual actions, they will succeed without effort when performed at that time. (Mmk 18.73)
The zodiac signs have been designated as jars by the sages of old;
both Bhadrapadas are renowned, and Revatī is illustrious.
Likewise, the eastern direction, though lacking limbs, is marked by auspicious planets such as Indra;
all these are praised and beautiful, and that field should be given to the Guru.
Thus has it been told in summary regarding the sign of Pisces by those marked by the world:
the planet is everywhere predominant, whether horizontal or liberated, in all ritual actions.
These seven classes of superior non-human beings have indeed been described in the context of the arrival of the planetary hosts.
The chief planets are infinite, as are the contemptible planets;
these have been declared to be neutral, bringing both benefit and harm to human beings.

Thus, for those who recite mantras, the application of sentient beings has been explained; likewise, the presence or absence of sentient beings, as well as the time and the specific rule, have been proclaimed. (Mmk 18.78)
There is no grasping associated with the dharma, nor is there action marked by the planets;
the conjunction of the planets and constellations is declared to be the accomplishment of mantra.
Success is not to be known as time, nor is failure said to be time;
both of these, success and failure, arise sequentially from attachment and time.
Those who delight in the contrary are not practitioners of Dharma; they are not true followers of the Dharma.
One who is joined through the union of the Dharma and ritual action will achieve success;
for one who is devoid of action, there is no success, nor does success arise from fate alone.
Both that action and its accomplishment depend solely upon destiny;
for there is no action apart from destiny, and destiny is nothing other than action.
But it is held that the [planets] are subject to karma due to the causes indicated by the rules;
yet the planets are liberated from karma, as are the well-worshipped lunar mansions.
Therefore, their action is equal; success is desired for the sake of the action.
For these enumerations have been taught, and action itself is always accompanied by the deities.
Neither the planets, the zodiac signs, nor the birth-constellations, even when well-worshipped, [determine one's fate];
one should always know that it is karma which is proclaimed as being liberated from ritual rules.
The arising of results is always dependent upon ritual action; this method has been taught regarding mantras.
Therefore, through this method, there is neither a seizing [of the result] nor any birth from a planet or a zodiac sign.
In brief, the movement and origin of the constellations and lunar days,
as well as the regulation of the measure of time, are always dependent upon the two types of karma and nothing else.
Therefore, one who knows the tantras should apply himself solely to the Dharma;
for in this world, there are various other infinite hosts of malevolent spirits. (Mmk 18.88)
The lunar days have been calculated in number by those who apply the fields;
therefore, I shall speak in brief—listen to what is being told.
Aries, Taurus, Gemini, and well-yoked Cancer;
as well as Leo, Virgo, Libra, and the other two, Scorpio and Sagittarius.
The Makara and the Kumbha are to be known [as such], while the others are the Mīna and the Vānara;
the Mānuṣa and the Devarāśi, and another is the Garuḍa. Mmk_18.91 //
The hosts of yakṣas and rākṣasas, as well as animals, pretas, and others who are auspicious,
and the hells— these are designated as the infinite realms of existence born from the various modes of birth.
All the astrological houses (rāśis) arising from various elements have been taught;
the sages have declared that there are innumerable other houses of many kinds.
I have explained the signs of their courses and the basis for the birth-places of sentient beings; now I shall speak further of the infinite lunar mansions and planets,
and the many fields that are said to be inhabited by various planets.

Thus ends the second chapter, the section on the knowledge of astrology concerning the characteristics of planets, lunar mansions, fields, and luminaries, from the sixteenth detailed exposition of the *Āryamañjuśrīmūlakalpa*, a Mahāyāna Vaipulya Sūtra that is an ornament of the Bodhisattva-piṭaka.
(Vaidya 138) Now begins the nineteenth chapter.
Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni, having again gazed upon the abode of the Śuddhāvāsa gods, addressed Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta.

"Mañjuśrī, there is also a third chapter on the rules of astrological knowledge that I shall speak; it was spoken and approved by the previous Perfectly Awakened Ones, and it is formulated for the purpose of your mantra-tantras.
Listen well, and attend to it thoroughly."

When the Blessed One Śākyamuni had spoken thus, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta rose from his seat, draped his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee upon the ground, and [turned] toward where the Blessed One was.
Having joined his palms in reverence,
he said this to the Blessed One:
"It would be well, O Blessed One, if the Blessed One would speak on the extensive section concerning the knowledge of astrology."
That shall be for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of sentient beings—
of gods and humans, and of those beings who have entered into all mantra practices, as well as those who have set out toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
They will easily accomplish the practice of mantras through skill in means;

it will be in accordance with all sentient beings, conforming to the performance of yoga rituals, resulting from the determination of time, and governed by the principle of karma as one's own making. It will be the method for easily accomplishing [the goal], following the mantras and having a pleasant maturation; it will be the miraculous display and the empowerment of supernatural power (*ṛddhyadhiṣṭhāna*) of those bodhisattvas, taking into account the lunar mansions, days of the week, planets, birth-classes (*yoni*), fields, zodiac signs, and their collective conjunctions.
When Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta had spoken thus, the Blessed One then said this to Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta:
"Excellent, excellent, Mañjuśrī! It is well that you ask the Tathāgata about this matter."
"In that case, listen well and attend thoroughly;
I shall speak for the benefit of all sentient beings.
When this had been said, Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta prostrated at the feet of the Blessed One.
He sat down to listen to the Dharma.
Then the Blessed One, having pervaded the entire abode of the Śuddhāvāsa deities with his radiance,
entered the samādhi called "The Illumination that Beholds All Buddhas.
As soon as the Blessed One had entered this state, rays of light— blue, yellow, white, madder-red, crystal-colored, and so forth— issued forth from his body.
Having emerged and illuminated the buddha-fields of sentient beings,

he illuminated all the planets, constellations, origins, lunar mansions, stars, and palaces; and having reached the vault of the sky, he illuminated the abodes of hell-beings, animals, hungry ghosts, gods, and humans— the dwellings of all sentient beings.
Having allayed all sufferings, it once again vanished within the work of the Blessed One Śākyamuni for the sake of all sentient beings.
Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni, having arisen from that samādhi, addressed all those assemblies of deities of the lunar mansions, planets, and constellations:

"Listen, O you assemblies of deities of all the lunar mansions! Whoever has entered into the practice of mantras within this Dharma-vinaya and seeks to accomplish [the goal] here in this detailed ritual manual, you must not create obstacles for them regarding any of the mantras; rather, all of you who have gathered here must declare your presence and provide protection."

For whoever should transgress this samaya, Yamāntaka, the King of Wrath, would instantly summon all the lunar mansions and planets— those residing in infinite world-systems along with their sons, kinsmen, and retinues;
standing upon the heads of them all and treading on them with his foot, he would display various miraculous feats of fierce magical power.
By the Buddha’s empowerment, he deprived him of life,
established him in the samaya,
and manifested himself in a transformed form.
In front of him were all the hosts of bhūtas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, nakṣatras, grahas, and rāśis, along with the multitudes of niḥsattvas, garuḍas, maruts, and mahoragas;
they were all terrified,
trembling, and shaking with fear.

Uttering a great cry of lamentation, they fell at the feet of the Blessed One and, trembling, spoke thus: "Save us, O Blessed One! Save us, O Sugata! We are without a protector; we are without a refuge."
"O Great King of Wrath, terrified with fear, may the Blessed One grant us our lives!
Having spoken thus, they became silent, their limbs trembling.
Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni addressed that assembly of constellations and planets, as well as the hosts of yakṣas, rākṣasas, pretas, piśācas, and mātṛs:
"Do not fear, sirs! Do not fear, sirs! For those who have approached the presence of the Tathāgatas, there is no fear nor death."
For all sufferings are to be warded off, O friends: one should go for refuge to the Buddha;
one should go for refuge to the Dharma, the foremost among those that protect from calamity;
one should go for refuge to the Saṅgha, the foremost among those free from passion.

He does not experience even a hair-raising thrill when praised as the foremost among the hosts; rather, he desires the truth and speaks accordingly. He should be regarded as one who has indeed been liberated from the fear of death and from all fears and sufferings;
no worldly fear ever exists for him.
May he attain that state which is the pacification of suffering, peace, freedom from fever, well-restrained, and directed toward awakening.

Then, at that very moment, the Blessed One dispelled all their sufferings through his miraculous power (*ṛddhi*). And Yamāntaka, the King of Wrath, prostrated at the feet of the Blessed One and sat down near Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta to listen to the Dharma. All those hosts of planets and constellations, as well as all their sufferings, were completely stilled.

And all the banners were stilled; they sat down to listen to the Dharma, having become composed, with one-pointed minds, gazing at the Blessed One with eyes wide open in wonder, their hearts filled with amazement.

Then, out of compassion for the world, the Blessed One gave a teaching of the Dharma in such a manner, associated with the Four Noble Truths, that by those beings some perceived the Truths, some attained arhatship, some attained the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha,
and some generated the resolve for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.

And all [beings] were rendered certain regarding unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment; by all of them, the doors to rebirth among gods and humans were opened, while the gates to the lower realms, evil destinies, and perdition were closed,
and the bolt on the way to heaven was removed.
And all empower the pledge.

Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni, having understood their underlying tendencies and immediately recognizing that the time for their discipline had arrived, taught the Dharma to those beings who were ready to be tamed.
Overcome by the suffering of enemies, devoid of a basis born of faults,
and non-existent— all these hosts of gods are worshipped here in this teaching.
Exert supreme vigor for the sake of the steps to enlightenment;
thus, O assemblies, you shall surely attain the abode that is peaceful and free from fever.
Nirvana is sorrowless, stainless, secure, and ultimate;
it is called immaculate and equal to space, for its intrinsic nature is non-existence.
"You shall attain the supreme, blameless, divine, well-frequented, and unobstructed state;
by meditating day and night upon all things as impermanent, suffering, empty in meaning, and selfless, you will indeed attain the ultimate goal."
Through the exposition of mantra and tantra, the practice that brings about happiness has been taught by the supreme Victors; it is declared to be the most excellent, the accomplishment of mantra.

The wise ones have taught the accomplishment of mantras as the foremost means for sentient beings, through their certain application at the time of the fruit’s attainment and the arising of the result.
The variety of births is joined by the variety of actions;
from action comes diverse accomplishment, for the manifold world is born from action as its source.
Variegated by means of these mantras in their variegated forms, the extensive ritual activities possess variegated purposes; thus it is called "variegated action."
Karma is thus both conceivable, in its manifold variety, and inconceivable, yet it is also conceived;
therefore, the mantra-practitioner should undertake abundant success within the diverse applications of mantras.
The zodiac signs have been described; among them are always born men, as well as the leaders of gods and asuras, and various living beings and birds.
And one should apply their respective signs to the attainments (siddhis).
Thus, whether they be humans or gods, those born under the zodiac sign of Aries [possess these characteristics].
Such a person is described as having many children, being eloquent, and handsome;
he is a merchant by character, as well as brave among men and women.
The Moon situated there is said to be crooked and of a greedy mind toward those who serve the king; one should employ it in all rites.
If the sun should be seen situated in the zodiac sign of Aries,
there, rites joined with cruel actions will always achieve success.
One who knows the tantras and mantras should never resort to vehicles, walking, sitting, or sleeping that are opposed by all yogins;
for a mortal born therein should always bestow a mantra intended for malevolent rites.
A person born then under the sign of Taurus is always possessed of enjoyments;
he is beloved by women, ever covetous, and a judge of what is righteous and unrighteous.
One who frequents villages and is always presiding over them should understand the limbs of the deity;
established therein, he becomes the Moon, that righteous Lord of the Gods.
The mind of one who always takes refuge in the kingdom should indeed be such;
to him, the mantras spoken by the Jina at the caityas should always be given.
By that [mantra] joined with the meaning of the moon, the bases of the syllables are understood;
the activity of going and coming, as well as the grooming of the beard, is endowed with logical consistency.

One should perform the rites of planetary influence, but one should not carry out malevolent magic; rather, one should apply oneself to all ritual activities that bring about the blissful arising of mantra-siddhi. (Mmk 19.20)
One should draw mandalas and the like, and have images of the Buddhas fashioned;
the best of divine substances for accomplishment are the spirits who are being propitiated.
When joined with mantras, they are accomplished by practitioners under the very lunar mansions and among the ṛṣis.
When a human is born under the asterism Mithuna,
then listen to the signs of their destiny and the time of their accomplishment regarding those who dwell in heaven.
One is born wealthy, diligent in mind, yet deceitful and foolish;
if one is renowned while situated there, it is like the stars adorning the night sky.
Then, that mortal becomes beloved by his kin, always dear to them, wealthy, endowed with ingenuity, and is known as a great lord.
By the remaining malefic planets and various other contemptible ones,
one is born as a rogue, afflicted by passion and overwhelmed by diseases.

Indeed, his mantras—whether for pacification (*śāntika*), enrichment (*pauṣṭika*), or the supreme [rites]—will not succeed; nor will those for minor [purposes], nor those that cause dejection, nor those of the flesh-eating, corpse-consuming [spirits].
Furthermore, he will always have visions of cruel, preeminent planets.
For the sake of accomplishing these mantras, one should employ them in cruel rites;
however, going there is forbidden, except for the foremost five.
In all ritual actions there, there is no success in going or coming;
likewise, for those [beings], one should bestow only minor rites, knowing them thoroughly in every respect.
Those two chief planets known as white are auspicious, while the other two are sinful;
the fourth aspect among the chief planets brings about the arising of prosperity.
Both red and both black are the appearances of those who perform cruel deeds;
white are those with faces like the bright moon, while yellow are Mercury and Jupiter.
Arka and Aṅgāraka are both red, born from the earth in the [southern] direction;
Ṣaṇḍa and Rāhu are likewise black; the remaining planets are variegated.
They are said to be possessed by various grahas, diverse and well-adorned with bodily elements;
some have variegated forms, while others are intent upon various weapons.
Presided over by various hosts of deities and ancient seers,
all the planets are attended by apsarases and kinnaras.

Those who dwell in the sky have attained their state through their color; they are known by their modes of movement and origins, all moving through the intermediate space together with the constellations.
Arriving in the sky with various movements and gestures,
they possess great supernatural power (*maharddhika*) through their majesty, by virtue of their gait, form, and attire. (Mmk 19.35)
These have been taught by all the best of sages, joined with the true meaning of ritual action;
they are to be employed on the fourth day and applied to the four types of sentient beings.
Four excellent planets have been declared: the white and the yellow are for accomplishing worldly aims;
the remaining ones are for cruel rites, and the red and black are likewise employed there.
One should not perform any rites, especially those for pacification,
on these two days when the planets are black and red, and also on the fourteenth lunar day.
One should not perform all [other] activities; one should accomplish minor rites.
A seeker of goals should accomplish auspicious calculations regarding human affairs.
With those very [materials], the wise one should always quickly have a seat, a bed, and a temple made; he should enter [the temple] and have all difficult passages constructed.
A person born under the sign of Cancer is seen to be auspicious;
he shall quickly become a teacher and even a universal monarch (cakravartin).
O venerable ones, for living beings, consciousness arises from the emergence of past karma,
and likewise the vision of the Moon, Indra, the planets, and the foremost [deities] occurs.
On an auspicious day and in an auspicious place, the Bodhisattva was born;
through conjunction with the Puṣya constellation, those honored by the gods are born.
The Buddhas, the teachers of the three worlds, and others possessed of great supernatural powers;
kings who rule kingdoms and those who destroy them, lords of many living beings.
In this world, various beings are born marked by Saturn, the Sun, and Mars;
some are mortals who are densely populated with people and devoted to their duties.
Those born under Puṣya are always born with various modes of conduct;
therefore, know that the fruit of karma is the destiny resulting from one's own actions.
However, those who follow right conduct and are engaged in the rites of the planets,
disregarding worldly concerns here, teach in that manner, just as the Victors have taught.
Karma is the diversity of the world, born from the meditative absorption of the world-system;
it is the vessel for all worlds, the source and origin of their manifestation.
"O gods, best of beings, understand that which has been told in the world as manifold;
for even in the past, the Compassionate One spoke of that which is born of karma."
Then the wise Bodhisattva Mañjughoṣa, possessed of great supernatural power and common to all beings, made this choice out of a desire for the welfare of sentient beings.

Everything arising from karma has been explained in detail within the mantras and tantras; O all you gods, this is indeed the Dharma that is always [attained] by means of a single [method]. (Mmk 19.51)
For one born under the zodiac sign of Cancer, it bestows a mantra for nourishment;
thereafter, the sign of Leo appears to the man.
A mortal born under Siṃha will be a hunter of sheep;
he will be deceitful toward women, a consumer of meat, and a dweller in mountain caves.
Likewise, the king, as the great supervisor and commander-in-chief, should always cause the earth to be governed; he is one whose actions are stern yet who is ever pure.
Ungrateful, one who betrays secret counsel, constantly devoted to evil deeds,
a traitor to friends, ever-greedy, and deceitful— thus he was born.
If it is always aspected by white or yellow planets that are wise, one born there becomes righteous; if by black ones, he is considered deceitful.

Therein, the rite for prosperity (pauṣṭika) has been taught for those desiring success, as well as the rites for rising up, moving through the air, and attaining the state of one who has transcended the mind.
One should not undertake another rite, nor should one avoid that which is similar;
beyond that, the Lion [sign] is known as the sign of Virgo.
One born there will be a rogue, a thief, miserly, and deceitful;
always lustful toward women, greedy, cruel, and perpetually reckless.
One who is foolish, an adulterer, stubborn, and always puffed up with pride [is not successful],
even when auspicious lunar mansions and days are present, and when there are auspicious aspects and the rising of favorable planets.
Those seen by planets that are yellow or white are born very wealthy;
they possess pure mantras, are always wise, and abide in pure conduct.
One should accomplish on the surface of the earth those mantra-tantras that have arisen,
which quickly bring about one's aims and those which are proclaimed for the sake of nourishment.
The knower of mantras shall accomplish all [rites] belonging to the families of the limbs of the Jinas,
as well as those mantras of the foremost Lords of Jinas that have been proclaimed in many ways.
The knower of mantras shall accomplish all things within the signs and their respective classes;
beyond that, the sign known as Libra (Tulā) occurs.
One should not resort to that which is well-known for being dominated by ritual action and dependent upon it;
for the wise one, when applied to the attainments of mantra, is born equal to the balance.
One should not perform any ritual practice that arises from or is bound to the earth;
for the sake of accomplishing all mantras, one should practice within the various states of existence and wombs.
One born under the zodiac sign situated in Libra is seen to be always devoted [to it], yet becomes deceitful, wretched, greedy, and indeed envious. (Mmk 19.67)
The practitioner of mantra, having resorted to that lunar mansion, should always perform it;
for in this world, they do not speak of any other ground for the attainment of wealth and prosperity.
When the moon is in conjunction with the chief of the planets (Jupiter), one born at that time will be surrounded on all sides by yellow and white [attendants];
yet he shall not attain success in mantra, nor achieve the wealth and prosperity sought through diligent effort.
When all this is being accomplished in a mere moment by those who are directed [to it], and when it is seen on all sides by auspicious planets that are yellow or white; Mmk_19.70.
A great-souled hero, righteous, or a lord of men is born when one is aspected by extremely cruel planets: Saturn, the Sun, Mars, or those born in Leo.
If the meaning of the sign is Libra, the man becomes envious,
afflicted by many diseases, and poor, arising from the torment of illness and disease.
One who is fierce in all actions, cruel, and always impulsive should not perform rites for pacification, as taught by the Lord in the section on the reality of the Jinas.
One performs fierce rites for the wielder of the thunderbolt that arise from the assembly,
as well as rites of sorcery and various acts of warfare.
In that heap, always in that family and born from that [source],
even a contemptible act attains success there through the supreme Victors.
One should avoid the expansion of primary qualities and powers,
and one should not undertake travel abroad toward the direction of Mārajit.

One should not perform any rites whatsoever— whether for the sake of the vehicle or for the manifested or unmanifested realm of sentient beings— while the sun is situated in that [Mandara] constellation.
When [the mantra] arises from a scorpion, one should take recourse in the womb of a sentient being;
listen now as the various signs that occur are described.
Such a mortal is born upon the surface of the earth as one who is fierce, reckless, cruel, irrepressible, arrogant with pride, crooked, and greedy.
A mortal shall be wise, righteous, learned, yet crooked and difficult to approach;
he shall be beloved by women, grateful, and firm in his prowess.
Constantly engaged in the practice of tantras and mantras, devoted to service, and honoring the guru;
[the planets] Venus, the Moon, Mercury, and Jupiter are the principal grahas for the vision [of success].
It is praiseworthy, conducive to the highest good, a worthy goal, and increases longevity and health;
it is for the sake of accomplishing the vision of those [deities] by means of the higher practice of the mantra-practitioners.
When Saturn, the Sun, Mars, and Rāhu behold that man,
he becomes cruel, impulsive, perverse, and a performer of fierce deeds.
And for those practitioners of cruel rites, the mantras of the Vajra-holder will be accomplished;
no mortal shall come from any quarter during even the most contemptible days.
Beyond that, mortals are born in many ways according to their destination and location, as the Tathāgatas have declared regarding the zodiac sign called Dhanus.
And all those who were beautiful in their youth became partakers of suffering;
thus have the designations of the divisions of lifespan been proclaimed according to their respective portions.
Likewise, I shall describe the accomplishment of wealth and the attainment of prosperity;
[yet] it will constantly destroy one's own source and cause the source of others to increase.
A mortal who takes refuge in the sign of Sagittarius will have many wives, be talkative, be fond of various passions and pleasures, and remain unrestrained.
If there is a sight of the principal planets that are white or yellow, one is born as a lordly, illustrious, always capable, and even righteous person.
One should practice their mantras, which arise from various weapons,
or those having the results of various arms, as well as those consisting of garments, ornaments, and vehicles.
Furthermore, the mantras produced from the limbs favored by the Munis— those formed according to various elements and arising as the fruit of various elements— will indeed be accomplished for him.
Thereafter, the mantra-practitioner should cause all rites to be performed with all substances; thus he shall produce, in every respect, a state of rebirth that is free from calamity.
One's own home, as well as one's vehicle, one's daughter, one's dwelling,
all desired things, great wealth, and that which leads to higher realms.
For his success, the liberated soul quickly stands in his hand;
thereafter, in the sign of Capricorn, he is seen equally situated in the assembly.
A mortal born among them may always recognize [them] by these signs:
he is devoted to his mother, devoted to his father, renowned, highly esteemed, and a leader.
He was unbearable amidst all sufferings; though wealthy, he was a hoarder of riches;
he became a miser with a greedy mind and likewise deceitful.
When planets are aspected by Venus or Jupiter, all prosperity arises;
however, those planets that are black or red bring about cruel deeds, as previously described.
The knower of mantras should not go there from any of the intermediate directions;
he should accomplish malevolent rites and avoid those that are undesirable.
One should resort to the northern direction for the purpose of inducing vomiting;
for the sake of reaching the great ocean, one should embark upon a boat for goods.
There, one shall obtain prosperity arising from the region of the presiding deity of the nadir;
beyond that is Kumbha, following after the rising of Makara.
Those born under the sign of Aquarius are always characterized by a multitude of natures;
they have been described by the best of men as possessing many forms and many marks.
Variegated and of diverse forms, by virtue of their reliance on caste and birth,
men of dark complexion and large eyes are born highly esteemed.

Those born in the zodiac sign of Aquarius (Kumbha) are said to be incapable of sexual intercourse, yet they contemplate the purposes of worldly conduct; they are grateful and righteous, and are practitioners of mantra.
In this world, planets that are white or yellow are seen and highly honored;
however, those planets that are black or red arise from the manifestation of their innate nature.
Men are always born with missing limbs, wretched, foolish, fickle, prone to theft, afflicted by many diseases, and impoverished. Mmk_19.105(=“114“)
One should not have them perform the supreme rite honored by the sages,
by which they might give rise to obstacles in all ritual actions.
One should not go even after reaching the edge of the shore; therefore, it has not been described [further].
One should perform the rites of the Vajra family with the desire to attain the siddhi of mantra.
One should accomplish here the mantra that is fierce, with a cruel conclusion, adorned with the syllables *sphaṭ* and *huṃ*, and properly joined with the King of Wrath;
those who perform sinful deeds succeed when they are applied to these rites of terrible action.
Beyond that, the Tathāgatas have declared the sign of Pisces;
all the young men situated there are seen to possess many marks.
Those born under the sign of Pisces (Mīna-rāśi) manifest these characteristics:
they are lords, possessed of honor and intelligence, illustrious, endowed with a hundredfold wealth and enjoyments,
and they arise on this earth as masters of all the worlds.
Then a wise king was born who swiftly accomplishes his aims;
born from the sight of the moon of Śukra, he becomes the best of men in the world.
From the sight of wise living beings, one becomes wealthy;
moreover, with a tall stature and large eyes, one shall always be beloved by women.
One who has many enemies becomes a ruler of men and likewise crooked;
whereas one with many friends becomes bright and affectionate toward friends.
Beyond that, if the cruel Divākara, the foremost of planets, together with Śani,
Rāhu, and Bhauma, beholds those mortals— (Mmk 19.114).
At that time, the banner becomes miserable and cruel;
for these planets have been described as before during the dark and light fortnights.
One should perform all rites while relying on the zodiac sign of Pisces;
situated therein, one should observe the moon and accomplish everything.
Beyond this, there are the hosts of elephants, humans, and non-humans,
as well as gandharvas, rākṣasas, garuḍas, and pannagas.
Their mental manifestation, characterized by their essential nature, genus, destiny, and location,
should be recognized by these very signs.
Just as the nature of a being is, so is its *liṅga* explained;
for these [beings] have their own mantras spoken, and one should employ those very [mantras] for them.
In the world, the twelve zodiac signs are said to have originated from the Gaṇas;
they are calculated by the foremost of the planets and joined with the lunar mansions.
These have indeed been described in brief, for they would be too extensive to recount in full;
at that time, they were established by the circles of planets among the lunar mansions for human beings.

On the first day of the bright fortnight, one should likewise favor the third;
as well as the fifth, the seventh, and those arising on the tenth and eleventh.
Likewise, on the thirteenth day of the bright fortnight, one should perform all rites:

likewise, the wise person [should employ] ornaments, vehicles, dwellings, and even the art of shaving.

Although various other rites have been taught by the foremost of Sages as being distinct from one another,

... [accompanied] by the Moon, Venus, Jupiter, and Mercury, with these most excellent, divine planets, well-honored, pure, and auspicious.

The planets, the meanings of the zodiac signs, the lunar mansions, and the lunar days have been fully explained,

Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni, having again gazed upon the abode of the Pure Abodes, addressed Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta.

Mañjuśrī, in your *Kalpavisara*, there are described signs and marks that dispel all causes of fear; these marvelous signs indicate auspicious and inauspicious events, such as the onset of famine or plenty, the invasion of foreign lands, drought, or excessive rain, thereby foretelling the condition of sentient beings. Mantras joined with the prescribed ritual procedure are certainly not desired when they are deficient, even for a high-souled Brahmā; how much less so for humans on earth?
Even for the god Śakra, for Rudra the wielder of the trident,
for Viṣṇu with the discus and mace in hand, and even for the high-souled Tārkṣya—
success shall not be attained by them through rites performed devoid of the prescribed rules.
When a mantra is well-recited and joined with the causes prescribed in the tantra,
it succeeds even for another person.
When released by humans according to the ritual procedure, adorned with the reality of the vidyā,
and applied at the proper times, they— along with the grahas— attain accomplishment when cast and recited.
Knowledge applied everywhere bestows results;
knowledge, which consists of causes, actions, and fruits, is that which refutes [wrong] causes.
One should know that action is accompanied by a cause; one should understand that from the arising of cause and fruit comes knowledge.
One should apply knowledge to the fruit of action, and likewise join other causes.
Likewise, the fourth vidyā, when applied to the four types of rites, bestows the fruit of the rite swiftly; that vidyā is joined with its specific cause.
That vidyā should be known by its fruit as being highly honored even by the Buddhas;
it is endowed with all purposes, preeminent, and effective for all rites.
When applied to ritual actions, that vidyā bestows success through those rites;
it shall lead one toward the highest good, for it is beyond the scope of ordinary mantras.
Understand the power, the accomplishment of mantras, and the true nature of the world;
as well as how action may be fruitless, or how action and its fruit exist therein.
Furthermore, the cause and fruit [of practice] are seen to be established according to the principles of the world; thus have the mantras been described by the Buddhas.
Fruit does not destroy action, nor does fruitless action destroy subsequent activity;
from the undertaking of action comes fruit, and success arises through mantras.

Because the sequence of qualities is not joined with substance, and the sequence of substance is not joined with action, the King of Mantras is accomplished therein; the fruit is applied to the ritual actions.
One who is endowed with the prescribed materials, established in right conduct, and engaged in ritual action—
such a person is not to be known as "born" from karma, for he is always joined to the fruit through his application.
They do not attain great power or the perfection of mantra-syllables at all times;
therefore, the practitioner of mantra should recite the mantra by relying on the source of the ritual procedure.
The sequence of time, the qualities, the ritual rules, the source, the destinies, and the path of the Sugatas—
all these kings of mantras are accomplished when they effect the purpose of the ritual and the time.
A quality (guṇa) is not to be known as a substance (dravya), nor is a quality said to be non-substantial;
through the conjunction of quality and substance, and by means of their union, one should worship the mantra.
One should employ all the deities who have been worshipped by means of the very face [of the mantra];
one shall quickly accomplish the measure, the quality, and the substance within the mantras.
The sequence endowed with the qualities of time, the action of the sequence of qualities and time—
success is seen to be fourfold when well-applied within the mantras.
When applied to virtuous qualities, mantras bestow everywhere power, the expansion of virtues, and the arising of happiness through the conduct of sentient beings.
The efficacy of all ritual actions is accomplished through qualities and substances;
yet these qualities do not exist apart from substances, nor do they exist devoid of substance and action.
Those mantras prescribed for the mind do not grant accomplishment quickly through mere mental intent alone; nor do they function through speech without the mind. (Mmk 21.94)
Nor is it to be known through mantras by another means, nor is it other than the mind;
there is no other action, and accomplishment is held to arise from the conjunction of the mind alone.
One is not deficient in the action of right view, nor is that which is devoid of action desired;
thus, right view, as well as action, speech, and mind, are properly applied.
The deities are swiftly accomplished when they are proclaimed through the syllables of mantra and tantra,
for one who is endowed with right view and who applies himself to right action.
Furthermore, mantras always succeed perfectly when they are endowed with the excellence of the conclusion of the ritual action and speech, and are properly joined with right view.
Mantras are accomplished in every way when properly applied to their respective ritual actions;
yet there is no mantra without the mind, nor is there [success] without mindfulness, for these two are inseparable from the mind.
Through right mindfulness and within the mind, the accomplishment of mantras is seen;
the Tathāgatas have declared that a mantra is not effective when it is devoid of mindfulness.
When properly applied through mindfulness and the state of meditative concentration,
they are seen to be empowered by mantras and brought to accomplishment through samādhi.
The cultivation of right concentration consists of mantras highly honored by the world;
these mantras are the application of that concentration, thoroughly permeated by it.
There, the kings of mantras are accomplished, as is the most abundant yoga; through perfect meditative absorptions, one should meditate upon the supreme mantra, beginning with meditation.
The mantras of the yogins are accomplished; success is not said to come from non-yoga.
That which was previously spoken by me has been correctly explained and well-applied.
The sages who are compassionate toward sentient beings have declared that success does not come otherwise;
a mantra correctly applied to the meaning of reality will not bear fruit without intentional resolve (saṅkalpa).
Mantras are accomplished through right intention when they are properly applied according to the ritual rules;
however, no king of mantras is honored at all when it is devoid of right intention.
Mantras are accomplished in every respect when employed with a correct livelihood;
it should be understood that the arising of happiness in mantras occurs precisely through right intention.
When correctly employed, the mantras attain purity in one’s livelihood;
those foremost mantras, when well-applied as prescribed on earth, bring about accomplishment.

One who is disciplined and delights in a pure livelihood should properly and correctly apply himself to the fruit; the mantra-practitioner, with a pure mind, should always remain in a state of purity while delighting in right conduct.
For one who is pure, whose actions are pure, and who conducts himself with purity in his final deeds, the pure mantras always succeed, whether the circumstances be defiled or undefiled. (Mmk 21.110)
The other mantras, as well as those others that have been proclaimed, the mantras of practitioners succeed; indeed, the mantras spoken among the *kravyāda* [flesh-eaters] are effective.
By Rudras, Viṣṇus, and the planets, as well as by Garuḍas of great supernatural power,
and by Yakṣas and Rākṣasas who sing [the praises], those mantras that are difficult to master are brought to fruition.
Even when recited by various hosts of spirits and piśācas,
mantras do not succeed on their own if they are deficient in the prescribed ritual, nor among those who delight in impure conduct.
When employed according to the prescribed rite, it swiftly grants success even amidst impurities;
therefore, one should not perform a mantra-deed devoid of the proper ritual procedure.
Mantras accompanied by outflows (*sāśrava*) are accomplished when properly applied through ritual actions;
likewise, those noble mantras spoken by the Buddhas are to be realized.
Their accomplishment is declared to be well-established within the paths themselves—
the Noble Eightfold Path, which is perfectly joined with the Four Truths.
This [practice] always consists of the four meditations and is based upon the four bases of psychic power;
however, the preeminent mantras taught by the Buddha are distinguished as the most excellent.
Indeed, the nature of mantras, as taught by the ritual rules, is an ineffable essence, possessing the same nature as the non-existence of space; so too is that of the Noble Ones of great majesty.

O dwellers of heaven, listen as I shall describe the methods for the vidyās, which are prescribed according to their respective stages and are devoid of the path to supernatural powers (siddhi). Mmk_21.119.
When one follows the path of the ten courses of wholesome action and speaks only what is well-spoken,
the divine mantras are accomplished through ritual action performed according to the prescribed rules.

Thus ends the fifth chapter, the detailed exposition on the instruction for the ritual application of mantras and the signs for the determination of the arising of [the deity], from the *Ārya-mañjuśrī-mūla-kalpa*, a Mahāyāna Vaipulya Sūtra which is an ornament of the Bodhisattva-piṭaka.
(Vaidya 177) Now begins the twenty-second chapter.
Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni, having again gazed upon the abode of the Śuddhāvāsa deities, addressed Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta:
Mañjuśrī, there exists within your *Mūlakalpa-paṭalavisara* a teaching entitled "The Chapter on the Instruction for Knowing the Signs and Sounds of All Beings.
I shall now speak it;
by knowing which, all sentient beings engaged in the application of the practice of all mantras will understand the proper and improper time for all mantras.
Listen to that; attend to it well and thoroughly;
I shall speak.

Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta rose from his seat, draped his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee upon the ground, and extending his joined palms toward the lion throne of the Blessed One Śākyamuni, circumambulated him three times, bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, and addressed the Blessed One as follows:
Therefore, may the Blessed One please explain that instruction on the knowledge of the cries of beings for the benefit of all sentient beings;
it will serve as a requisite for the regulation of all times for those who have entered the practice of all mantras, for the sake of attaining signs of accomplishment.
Now, O Blessed One, do as you deem the time right.
Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni gave his approval to Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, Mañjuśrī! It is well that you consider it necessary to question the Tathāgata on this matter.
Therefore, Mañjuśrī, listen; I shall explain."
When this had been said, Mañjuśrī prostrated at the feet of the Blessed One, rose up, and sat down to listen to the Dharma.
Then the Blessed One, having surveyed the entire assembly, entered the meditative absorption named "The Incitement by the Sounds of All Beings.

Immediately upon the Blessed One’s entry into that absorption, whatever sentient beings were dwelling in the infinite and boundless world-systems, they were all illuminated by the Buddha’s rays; and bowing their heads to all those Blessed Buddhas, [they beheld] those dwelling in the infinite and boundless world-systems.

Having honored the lion throne situated above the palace of the Pure Abodes belonging to the Blessed One Śākyamuni, they approached it; and by means of that [throne], they arrived at the Sahā world-system. Standing there, all the hosts of beings, through the power of the Buddha, manifested their own respective voices and drew near to the feet of the Blessed One in order to hear the Dharma.
Having bowed to and honored the Blessed One, we sat down in our respective places to listen to the Dharma.

Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Lion of the Śākyas, the son of the King of the Śākyas, instructed, inspired, and gladdened all those beings with a discourse on the Dharma; he gave such a teaching of the Dharma to all those lords of spirits and gods that some among them all conceived the resolve for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

Some were established in the state of a *pratyekabuddha*, some in the state of a *śrāvaka*; some perceived the Truths, and some realized *arhatship*. Some, abiding in the ten paths of wholesome action, made this vow:

"May I serve infinite Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, throughout infinite millions of eons, providing them with attendance, medicinal requisites for the sick, robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and all necessary articles."
"And we shall become destined for the enlightenment of a Buddha."

Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni, knowing the disposition of those beings, spoke this mantra called "The Superknowledge of the Sounds of All Beings," by the accomplishment of which all bodhisattvas and all beings would understand the speech of everyone situated within their respective spheres of experience in a single instant.
And what is that?
Homage to all Buddhas, whose teachings are unimpeded, who abide everywhere without limit, and who are possessed of great compassion.
Oṃ, homage to the All-Knowing One, svāhā!
The ritual procedure for this is as follows:
first, having gone to a great forest, subsisting on a diet of milk and barley-gruel, or roots, fruits, and vegetables, one should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times.
One who bathes three times a day and wears garments of bark must perform everything according to the previously mentioned ritual,
just as it is prescribed in the mantra-tantras arising from the Tathāgata family.
Then, having performed the preliminary service (*pūrvasevā*), one should commence the actual practice (*sādhana*) at that very spot upon reaching the end of one hundred thousand syllables.
Even without a cloth,
having prepared a fire-pit measuring two cubits in depth and four cubits in width, square on all sides, and having offered an *arghya* oblation with all kinds of flowers and fruits,
one should sit facing east upon a bundle of *kuśa* grass, kindle a new fire, and set it ablaze with wood from milk-exuding trees.
One should offer eight thousand oblations of *śrīphala* fruits smeared with curd, honey, and ghee,
at the three junctions of the day, for twenty-one days.
Then, having created a great radiance in the eastern direction, the Buddha, the Blessed One, approaches;
he then touches the crown of the practitioner’s head.
If the practitioner is not touched, at that very moment a voice issues from the Blessed One: "You have attained success; go as you wish."
Having done this, he disappears.

From that time forth, the practitioner becomes one endowed with the five superknowledges (*pañcābhijñā*), possessing a divine form of great power, following the conduct of a Bodhisattva, appearing as a youth of sixteen years, moving at will, and knowing the cries of all beings;
in a single moment he understands the speech of all beings, becomes powerful, and travels wherever he desires.
He lives for five thousand years.
The bodhisattva becomes irreversible;

through twenty entries into the means of accomplishment, one will certainly succeed—of this there should be no doubt. Even for one who has already accomplished [the goal], let him understand that he must not recite the mantra at the very beginning, in the middle, or at the end.
Now, the knowledge of sounds, their power, and their intrinsic nature are proclaimed.
In the midst, at the beginning, and indeed at the end of the dwellers of heaven.
That which was spoken is recited in the world, and it is celebrated in the Middle Country;
[the dialects] of Magadha are in the Maṅga countries, while those of the best of men are in the city of Kāśi.
Just as it was among the people in the midst of Vṛji, Kośala, and Madhya-deśa, so did the king of the gods choose all those mantras according to their inherent nature.
O Vatsa, behold how Tridaśa is in Madhyadeśa and Daśārṇava;
as it is in speech, so it arises in various regions.
Likewise, throughout all the Tridaśas, such speech was uttered;
and the Yāma deities, the chief gods, as well as the Nirmāṇarati and Paranirmita-vaśavartin gods [did so].
Then the speech uttered by the speaker, directed toward the meaning of the Middle Country,
was likewise understood by all those in Akaniṣṭha who possess great supernatural powers.
All those excellent deities, residing in the realm of form, subsisting on the food of meditative concentration and being serene, at times spoke these words.
She possesses the intellect of Brahmā and Īśvara; her voice is like the song of the kalaviṅka bird, a resonance of sweet syllables, and a sound like that of the intoxicated cuckoo.
Whatever speech there may be that is meaningful, endowed with courage and profundity,
and likewise entirely free from crookedness, is highly honored by the Visionary One.
O venerable ones, those gods in the Middle Country are always eloquent,
endowed with sweet syllables, and possessing a smooth, deep resonance.
Their speech is like the roar of clouds;
one should observe it as being honored among the people of the Middle Country, just as it is among those of Avanti.
One should likewise know the Mistress of the Gods (Sureśvarī) as being endowed with speech and sound;
she is produced from the sphere of non-perception (asaṃjñāyatana) by means of speech for those who are formless.
Due to the absence of a basis for them, the gods did not resort to speech;
all the most excellent gods are speakers in the Middle Country.
This speech proceeds as the sign of wealth for those in the Middle Country;
moreover, it concerns the gods, the earth-dwellers, and the yakṣas of great supernatural power.
Likewise, there are hosts of many beings who have entered into divine wombs,
as well as the Karoṭapāṇi gods and those always considered to be Vīṇakas.
The four great kings also rely upon the four modes of birth;
the thirty gods, the leaders of the deities, likewise rely upon them together with Śakra.
Furthermore, Suyāma and all those of beautiful form who dwell above,
as well as the most excellent hosts of all the gods— this speech is indeed proclaimed by them.
Just as mortals in the Middle Country are of low, superior, or middling [status],
so too is speech endowed with divinity of low, superior, or middling [quality].
Speech should be known as threefold: inferior, superior, and middling;
it should be known as threefold according to action: inferior, superior, and middling.

Likewise, in a temple, speech that is sweet and victorious through well-spoken verses, as well as the sounds and thoughts [of others], should be understood and employed specifically in ritual actions.
The speech of the *asuras* should always be that which originates from Gauḍa and Pauṇḍra;
just as the cry of the best among the Gauḍa people is adorned with sound,
so too should the best among the hosts of *daityas* employ their cry.
As they wandered about on all sides, there were the precursors of the yakṣas, rākṣasas, and pretas, as well as the nāgas together with the pūtanas;
[all these] belonging to the faction of the asuras, from the banks of the Vaṅgasa and Amata rivers.
One should likewise arrange [the offerings] for Harikeṭa, Kalaśamukhya, and Carmaraṅga, or indeed for all their provinces without exception.
One should never separate those three types as they have been described;
thus one should always proclaim them for the gods and for those who precede them. (Mmk 22.24)
The lords of the hosts of pretas and yakṣas, Skanda, the mātṛs, and kinnaras, as well as the nāgas—at all times, understand this according to my word. Mmk_22.25.
Just as it is in Lāḍa, Oḍra, and Sindh, so too in the north;
indeed, one should employ her among all people everywhere.
Just as the speech of the *nāgas* is said to be charming and wise,
so too is the speech of the *yakṣas* for those men who dwell in the northern direction.
Just as [the speech] of the Garuḍas is known among the Indras, and that of the Kinnaras is proclaimed, so too is the speech everywhere in Nepal; understand it to be just like that. Mmk_22.28 //
Likewise, the speech of *pūtanā* demons, of women dwelling in the womb of the Vindhya mountains, of men born in the Vindhyas, and of the *mleccha* barbarians; Mmk_22.29 //
That speech which has been proclaimed for them is to be known as belonging to the *pūtanas*;
the best of gods chose that very speech which belongs to the *rākṣasas*.
The southern regions are proclaimed to be among the Andhras and Lāṭas;
however, for all the Dravidians, [the speech] always abounds in the letter *ḍa*.
Having observed her speech, one should employ her among the rākṣasas;
thus, the three types of family origins of the rākṣasas are to be known.
This speech is indeed of three kinds, and one should employ it in a threefold manner;
it is to be known as threefold in every respect, and those regional dialects are likewise threefold.
One should likewise apply the threefold action to the three regions;
it is to be known as threefold in every respect, for the ritual action is traditionally taught to be threefold in its expression.
One should appoint another officiant there for all [the rites] equally;
various hosts of beings are proclaimed as those who dwell upon various parts of the earth.
And humans, possessing knowledge of many various languages and adorned with diverse sciences,
[teach] human lore expressed through various modes of speech.

The various doctrines of different treatises are to be known; they possess the meanings of various mantras, they present various instructions for ritual actions, and various accomplishments are thereby liberated.
When mortals who are possessed have come together at the place of the vessel,
they should be properly joined by means of mantras applied according to the ritual rules.
One should clearly visualize the deities as having arrived upon the surface of the earth through speech alone;
one should then assign the insignia, the meaning, the vessel, and the deity itself.
One should recognize the manifestations of those possessed as leading from excellence to even greater excellence;
they exhibit the customs of various lands and the emergence of various languages. (Mmk 22.40)
One should recognize various applications of ritual actions by their diverse characteristics;
for those whose speech outside the Middle Country is unstable, one should likewise discern them.
Those who are cruel, terrible Rākṣasas, and practitioners of fierce rites should clearly be known as men who are devoted to the languages of the Mlecchas.
Speech abounding in the sound "ḍa" and indistinct with the sound "la" belongs to the Mārṣas;
like the speech of those from the South, it is fickle and censured.
And likewise, among these, this speech is proclaimed for the Rākṣasas;
it is the Jyeṣṭhā, uttered in many ways, for those possessed by the three supreme ones.
Summoned swiftly by mantra-practitioners, or having come here of their own accord,
the Mothers and the gods together with the grahas seize sentient beings in many ways.
Garudas, yakṣas, gandharvas, kinnaras,
piśācas, uragas, rākṣasas, yakṣas, and pūtanas— [all these are subdued].
Likewise, listen as the characteristics of those possessed by them are described:
they speak the tongues of barbarians, are flesh-eaters, are Piśācas, and speak indistinctly. *Mmk* 22.47.
Speech abounding in the letter *la* and ending in the letter *ḍa* belongs to the Pūtanās;
their gaze directed upwards is employed in these rites.
Those who are stingy, cruel-natured, prone to falsehood, and delighting in impurity—their vision does not go upward; for they possess only half-vision and do not ascend.
Likewise, the speech of the Mothers is endowed with auspicious meaning;
the speech of the planets and the chief Kumāras is exclusively [of such a nature].
Possessing a perfection of beautiful limbs and speech joined with meaningful words for children,
his power is supreme in every respect, surpassing that of all the celestial dwellers.
One should observe the speech of the Garuḍas when they are possessed;
it should be known as being equal to the sound of the letter *ga*, appearing like the language of the Mlecchas.
"Unmanifest yet clearly appearing, endowed with fame, and the source of auspiciousness—
this [mantra], 'suparṇine pāyava,' is the destroyer of poison and pride."
For their future destinies, their various gatherings with beings of different natures, and their various colors are to be known; one should discern them by means of their various characteristics.
O Śubhākara, O Abhākara, you who shine forth, may the King of Nagas devour [the obstacles] at your feet!
Vāsuki and the other Nāgas, righteous upon the surface of the earth,
dwell as lords of serpents, endowed with swift speech.
One should identify each being according to their respective body and by whatever mark they may be characterized; by that very mark, one should designate each particular being.
All these are said to be degrading, for they are indeed characterized by downward vision;

they should be known as belonging to various classes of beings through the various types of bodily actions performed by those who have entered various bodies— understand them as having diverse physical forms.

Indeed, such various and manifold signs have always been described for mortals on earth who are possessed by [spirits], through actions performed with diverse intentions and based upon various wombs, as spoken by the one who speaks with many characteristics.

Just as the speech of the gods and the asuras indicates their respective purposes, so too should one quickly apply that [speech] when the earth has attained human form; then, with a very serene mind, one should know it to belong to the gods. (Mmk 22.59)
They gaze likewise upwards and in all directions,
undaunted in mind and free from agitation, joyful and endowed with beautiful forms.
One should observe that all these foremost of gods have pure eyes and unblinking eyes, they are smooth-skinned and have smooth faces, and likewise, they all possess a serene gait.
It should be known that some are seated upon a cross-legged posture on pure ground,
while others, having emerged from the sky, are seated as sky-goers.
The gods beginning with Brahmā are said to be absorbed in the joy of meditative concentration;
above them, in the abode of the most excellent, are those with form and those with manifold forms.
Drawn in by the mantras of the mantra-practitioners and supported by them,
their radiant form-bearing splendor— upon that very basis, I transform it.
Absorbed in the joy of meditative concentration, their faces are always slightly smiling;
with pure and wide eyes, they abide in many forms.
Then those gods, who possess splendor, glory, and perfect form,
and who know the supreme gnosis, shall instruct them.
Seated cross-legged and always meditating like a seer,
they understand through their intellect that possession brings about the accomplishment of desired aims.
One should employ this for the welfare of all mantras as the most excellent means;
O lords of the gods, understand that everything has been thus explained.
For these have been described by the Ṛṣis; they are self-controlled and established as Ṛṣis. I have thus described the signs of the Ṛṣis when they are possessed.
The gods have their gaze directed upwards; the Kaśmalas have their feet turned upward;
the Rākṣasas are deformed, of fierce appearance, and have hair standing erect. (Mmk 22.70)
Thus, among the Mothers, for whom indeed is this seen? The flesh-eaters stand naked, yet having been with clothing, they have become unclothed.
With their feet turned upward, known as the deformed ones, and with hair standing erect,
other seizing spirits roamed everywhere across the entire earth and the banks of the rivers.
At a solitary tree, in a cremation ground, at a single linga, on a sandy bank, in temples, on roads, in the valleys of the Vindhyas, and among mountain peaks; Mmk_22.73.

And even the peaked mountain of the Himālayas, along with the dwellings of barbarians and thieves, were drawn there by the power of mantras; those beings of deformed appearance arrived, summoned by the spells.
They swiftly seize those living beings who are averse to purity and proper conduct;
out of fear, they may even go throughout the entire earth to devour those deluded by food.
In the world, they seize [beings] in many ways, afflicting them with many diseases;
they possess various transformed forms and wear diverse garments.
They swiftly seize the corpses and the urine-sleeping beings of living creatures;
their signs have been described, and their conduct has been clearly analyzed.
Speech has been previously described as the first sign on the surface of the earth;
likewise, the signs of those possessed among human beings have been clearly identified.
O best of gods, understand that these are the stable types found everywhere;
likewise, the signs of those possessed by spirits among men on this earth have been described.
He gazes constantly with affection, his eyes never blinking,
toward the most excellent of gods upon this earth, amidst the afflicted beings of the human world.
He chose the earth, speech adorned with a multitude of sounds and meanings,
and the dharma conducive to the highest good within the human realm, having reached the state of non-retrogression.
The foremost among the best of gods has gone; he should be known as the achiever of all aims.
That which was intended by the reciter has been understood by him while staying in the abode of the gods.
One should quickly inform the mantra-practitioner of all that has been thought;
this is correctly described as the divine possession upon the earth.
Even those who are unconscious are always drawn to the surface of the earth by mantras;
O gods, do not speak sweet words, for there is no sacrifice for those in haste.
Deprived of their excellence and rendered powerless, they remained resorting to silence;
there was nothing in their speech, nor in their minds, nor even in their pride.
Therefore, the practitioner of recitation should not draw that [person] in;
nor is it impossible for them to accomplish those mantras born of the Victors. (Mmk 22.86)
For those who heat themselves through the meaning of the recited mantras, nothing exists that cannot be drawn forth;
likewise, the noble ones are drawn forth by the noble mantras when applied with proper method.
The marks belonging to the noble ones, which arise from the rhinoceros-like śrāvakas, as well as those of the great-souled bodhisattvas who abide on the ten stages; Mmk_22.88.
Likewise, those well-adorned with pledges (samaya) are drawn forth by mantras,
as well as by the great female messengers (mahādūtī) and the uṣṇīṣas, which are appropriately joined with the colors of the Sage.

By the wise sons of the Buddha, born from the families of the lotus and the moon, by those called Vajra who are the foremost of mantras, and by the kings of wrath possessed of great supernatural power; Mmk_22.90.
Neither other worldly kings of mantras possessing great supernatural powers, nor those who know the samayas, are capable [of this], nor is the supreme Lord of Mantras [capable] among them.
To describe, to count, or even to go to that place where they always dwell— [it is impossible],
for their cause is set in motion by the power of time and concentrated karma.
Indeed, their cause, which is concentrated in karma, is drawn forth;
and their tantra is drawn forth by means of the pledges spoken by the Buddhas.
Therefore, one should not disturb them with effort, nor should one employ them in vain for worldly purposes;
those great-souled ones possess great supernatural power and are established upon the ten stages.
Indeed, all mantras were then unable to go where those Tathāgatas were; likewise, O you who are honored by the immortals, remember my command! Mmk_22.95.
Then all those who know the mantra for the purpose of reciting it shall come;
the signs of those who have been summoned will be human or non-human bodies.
Steadfast, with a pleasing complexion, and a skillful teacher of profound meaning;
having attained steadfastness and depth, he shall then have few tears.
Having been questioned by one whose mind was unwavering and who was preeminent among those who know the mantras,

he brought relief from the experience of great suffering.
Once again, they vanished from the body of the Blessed One Śākyamuni.

Having fully awakened all sentient beings, the Blessed One spoke thus: "Now, this knowledge of sounds, which is honored for its meaning and the Dharma, is to be mastered; and the Knower of the World spoke sweet words regarding calculation as well. (Mmk 23.1)
The word should be understood from its base form, adorned with its suffix;
by means of that [base], it becomes extensively expanded through the addition of suffixes, arising from verbal action.

Through the manifestation of both word and sign, the purpose of the Dharma is accomplished.

rather, that entity which arises from the word "cognition" is the sound that joins with the ultimate reality.

through the conjunction of root and suffix, a word conveys both the phenomenon (*dharma*) and its meaning (*artha*).

rather, it is through its connection with the cognition of the meaning that the wise know that word as a linguistic convention.

depending on those [conditions], those sounds, which possess excellent supports, were then distinguished.
That knowledge of words by which mantras are spoken according to their true meaning—
one should not understand that [meaning] merely through the sounds of the words, without the realizations (pratyaya) of the mantras.

one should not seek to see those auspicious mantras everywhere except through their causal conditions.
Know that to be neither a conjunction nor the accepted meaning of a grammatical gender or a sentence, which is empty of the cognition of objects and devoid of the [six] elements.
The movement of the *liṅga* is not taught as being born from causes, conditions, or elements;

A sentence is a word that culminates in the action directed toward a destination; beyond this, one who would always utter speech with a mind full of wonder regarding the word [is truly a speaker]. Mmk_23.13 //

The accomplishment of the purpose does not arise from the mere sound; rather, it is applied to the ritual signs (liṅgas). The sound uttered at the crown of the head is said to be adorned with the meaning of the syllable *huṃ*.
Everything depends upon conditions and relies upon a basis;
the palate, lips, and mouth are the basis for speech, while others manifest that basis.
The object of knowledge is approached through tranquility; the method is unerring;
the intellect is suchness; and the expanse is adorned with meaning.
The *dhātu* forms a conjunction, marked by the meaning of the suffix;
thus, the dental and palatal [consonants], as well as the labial, follow according to the science of phonetics (*śābda*).

Through the power of the mantra, understand that the straight-tusked one [Riju-kṣu] pervades all worlds, consisting of emanations and the activities of the elements, reaching to the very end of the physical basis. Mmk_23.18 //

these words and mantras arise everywhere from the source of grammatical inflection.
