it becomes gold of a thousand-fold transmutation.
Having performed the purification of the body, one should construct a caitya with one's own hands;
even one who has committed the five acts of immediate retribution attains success.
By means of a hundred thousand caityas, one becomes a universal monarch of the vidyādharas.
One who is learned in all treatises, endowed with all specialized knowledge, and remains for an eon—once passed away, he does not go to the states of woe for five hundred births.
He is born in increasingly superior central lands, possessed of all faculties, retentive of what he has heard, and remembers his past lives.
Without being asked, he obtains red arsenic (*manaḥśilā*), places it upon seven *aśvattha* leaves, and performs the accomplishment.
All those who hear or smell [this] at the time of twilight come under one's control.
One emerges having pierced through mountains, walls, and the ocean.

Having smeared a mandala measuring sixteen or eight cubits in a cremation ground, having placed a corpse with its head toward the north, having inserted a left-hand finger into its mouth, and having stepped upon its chest with the right foot—
One should recite the mantra until the corpse moves;
then, grasping that finger with one's hand, one gives it [to the corpse].
Having inserted it into the ring finger, whoever one commands comes.
Saying "Return!", he causes [the corpse] to return.
Having placed his foot upon the corpse—provided it is not decomposed and its limbs are intact—he should recite the mantra until the corpse rises.
Having drawn the mantra there with saffron on the eighth or fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, one who is observing the *poṣadha* vows and established in the observances [should perform this].

Being alone and unaccompanied by anyone, he should ascend a mountain peak; having avoided the guardians of the directions, he should smear an eight-cubit mandala and fashion a stūpa out of sand. Having performed worship according to his ability, facing eastward and holding a sword in his right hand with his arm raised, he should recite the mantra before the stūpa.
Once the syllables have vanished, one takes that leaf—which has become a sword and is blazing—and becomes a *vidyādhara* who travels wherever he desires.
He is invulnerable to all *vidyādharas*, unassailable by all beings, able to assume any form at will, and capable of remaining for an eon (*kalpa*). He sees for a thousand *yojanas*.

With cane leaves smeared with pungent oil, there is pacification; with rice from a *śāli* field, one gains the wealth of a mountain. With mustard seeds over which the mantra has been recited one hundred thousand times, one destroys demonic spells.
With an arrow over which the mantra has been recited eight hundred times, one causes thunderbolts, vajras, stones, and the like to fall wherever one desires.
With ashes over which the mantra has been recited seven times, in whichever direction one scatters them, a protection against arrows is established there.
By reciting [the mantra] one hundred and eight times, all thorns [of pain] are extracted.
For one who has performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*), one should recite it twenty-five lakhs of times before the painted image (*paṭa*).

Then, having consecrated with eight thousand recitations a fingernail-clippings, a palm-leaf, a sword, or a substance for protecting all crops—intended as a paste for two-footed beings, four-footed animals, insects, mice, and so forth—one should cast it into water.
One becomes invulnerable to all nāgas.
By reciting the mantra one hundred thousand times, whatever one desires—
that one releases from bondage.
During a solar eclipse, one should place ghee from a cow that has a calf of the same age into a copper vessel and recite the mantra as long as the eclipse lasts.
By drinking that, one is liberated from all diseases.

Furthermore, according to the previously mentioned procedure, one who observes the *poṣadha* vows should offer one hundred thousand oblations of rice flour mixed with resin (*sarjarasa*) at a reliquary (*caitya*) containing relics.
One obtains a thousand dīnāras.
One should offer eight thousand white mustard seeds smeared with ghee;
then she reveals the hidden treasure.
It should be undertaken:

having constructed at a shrine containing relics, or on a river flowing to the ocean, a shrine made of sand with the size of a Sugata’s span and containing the essence of dependent origination; then, being pure and observing the *poṣadha* vows, having performed worship according to one's ability, and subsisting on alms-food or sacrificial food (*haviṣya*).
Or one should recite it one hundred thousand times;
one then becomes capable of all rites.

By collecting [substances] from a great cremation ground, there is the binding of the cardinal and intermediate directions of the mandala and so forth, as well as the treatment for all poisons, the cleansing of afflictions, and the destruction of possession by grahas and fever.
One should recite [the mantra] when crossing a great river;
one crosses with ease.
By the mere act of recitation, one becomes honored by ferrymen, tax collectors, forest guards, and others.
In a dispute, one becomes the respondent.

By means of a thousand recitations over [water] that induces sleep, binds semen, and stops urine, and by means of eight thousand recitations over stakes of *khadira* wood, there is no subjugation by mantras.
Having made an image of butter, the size of a thumb-joint, from barley grains smeared with curd, honey, and ghee—
Having placed it upon a leaf of the *aśvattha* tree and pressing it with the hand, one should recite the mantra until it vibrates; then,
one should grasp it without touching it with the teeth.
At that very moment, she arrives in a beautiful form and grants all desires. Having kindled a fire with *bilva* wood, one should offer ten thousand oblations of *bilva* fuel-sticks.

One obtains enjoyments; in all ritual procedures, there is the binding of the mandala, the binding of the boundary, and the binding of the mouth against thieves, tigers, crocodiles, sharks, and water-monsters,
as well as the acquisition of hidden treasures.

Having gone to that place where the treasure is located, having fasted there, having smeared a mandala, and having kindled a fire with wood from the *bilva* tree, one should offer oblations of royal mustard seeds; thus, one obtains the treasure.
Desiring to bring a queen together with her retinue under one's control, one should fashion an image out of *kuśa* grass, grasp it with the left hand, and recite the mantra one thousand times;
she, along with her retinue, will become submissive.
To subjugate a Brahmin, one should offer eight thousand oblations of sesame seeds smeared with curd, honey, and ghee; he, along with his retinue, will be brought under control.
To subjugate a Kṣatriya, one should offer eight thousand oblations of barley mixed with curd, honey, and ghee;
he becomes submissive along with his retinue.
To subjugate a Vaiśya, one should offer eight thousand oblations of black mustard seeds.
He becomes submissive along with his retinue.
For the subjugation of a Śūdra, one should offer eight thousand husks of black rice into the fire;
he becomes submissive.
One should perform the homa alone for three days.
Having combined the ghee of that very Kapila cow with Mālatī flowers, one should offer seven oblations.
If one places white mustard seeds consecrated seven times upon someone's head, that person becomes submissive.
For the purpose of subjugating a king, one should fashion an image of him and, approaching it with the left hand, recite the mantra eight thousand times;
he, along with his retinue, will become submissive.
Having consecrated well-strained water, one should retain it for seven days.
Then, having ensured the cowherds are protected, one should have the cows milked.
Then, in a secluded place, one should recite mantras over that milk while it is in a jar.
After churning it, one should have a Brahmin girl grind lotus seeds, *tagara*, lotus filaments, and sandalwood together with honey.
Having made a pill, one should empower it with mantras along with betel leaf; whoever one gives it to becomes submissive.
Having recited the mantra over a flower garland, whoever one places upon their head becomes submissive.
Red sandalwood, *campaka* flowers, lotus filaments, red rice husks, *girikarṇikā*, seeds of *koraṇḍaka*, rice, black gram, *kuṣṭha*, *tagara*, and *turuṣka* oil—these should be taken in equal parts.
One should have it performed:
having kindled a fire with *jāti* wood, one should offer eight thousand *jāti* flowers smeared with curd, honey, and ghee;
one obtains five hundred *dīnāras*.
Having kindled a fire with mango wood on a riverbank, one should offer eight thousand oblations of *arka* fuel-sticks smeared with curd, honey, and ghee.
On the fifth day, one obtains five *dīnāras*.
Beginning from the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight until the fifteenth, one should offer eight thousand oblations of *aśoka* fuel-sticks smeared with curd, honey, and ghee.
One obtains one hundred dīnāras.
Having kindled a fire with *karavīra* wood, one should offer eight thousand oblations of *karavīra* creepers.
Beginning on the eighth day of the bright fortnight until the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight, one obtains a thousand dīnāras; one should offer eight thousand oblations every day.
"Up until the fourteenth day":

one who has performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*) and fasted for three nights should take a piece of wood six finger-breadths long from a tree struck by lightning and recite the mantra over it. One should thus appease an enraged royal family or an enraged friend by means of various ritual actions.

Having installed a cloth painting in a reliquary containing relics, and having bound that ritual stake with the three metals, one should place four jars filled with all medicinal herbs upon a bed of lotuses.
Treading upon that stake with the left foot and grasping it with the left hand, one should recite the mantra until it vanishes.
Saying "Hand," he does not let go of the hand;
from that, one should offer a great bali-oblation.
At dawn, one should eat pomegranate.
That stake becomes perfected;
if one buries it in a forest, it becomes a house that grants all desires,
and all necessary utensils attend upon it.

Having drawn it out, everyone should drink from it and bathe; then this same ritual service is to be performed again until the end of the entire night. At dawn, the monks designated for the Saṅgha are to be fed.
Having fed [the recipient], one should eat pomegranates prepared with ghee. Then,
as he approaches,
the fourteen branches of knowledge enter his mouth.
One who possesses a retentive memory,
having descended to a river flowing toward the ocean, should form a fist with the right hand and recite the mantra for thirteen days;
this will cause all those bitten by venomous creatures to rise up.
With a fistful [of the substance], one destroys all seizing spirits (graha),
being released by their will.
Having stayed for three nights beneath an Aśoka tree, one should offer eight thousand oblations of *marīca* pepper.
Having placed a single grain of *marica* in the mouth, if one gazes with unblinking eyes, that person becomes submissive.
Merely by recollecting [the mantra], one destroys all calamities.
If there is a woman who does not please [one], having taken her name and consecrated clarified butter (*ghṛta*) with the mantra, one should cause it to be given to her.
One becomes fortunate.
This is the Vajra-attainment (*vajrasādhana*).
Having fashioned a sixteen-finger-long three-pronged vajra out of *puṣpaloha* (flower-metal), one should descend into a river flowing to the ocean and offer one hundred thousand fragrant flowers.
The western flower comes forth, breaking through the current;
one should swallow it without touching it with the teeth. Day by day, one grasps five hundred knots.
Having performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*), one should recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times before the cloth painting.
Then, having gone to the place where the treasure is located, one should smear a jar made of *kālamūla* wood with all kinds of perfumes and fill it with water infused with white sandalwood.
Having consecrated it eight thousand times, one should place it at the site of the treasure.
The entire ground opens up;
a treasure remains at the height of a man;
it should be taken.
One should offer one hundred thousand fuel-sticks of *palāśa* wood;
one obtains a thousand cows.
One should offer one hundred thousand *śephālikā* flowers.
One obtains the desired object.
One should offer one hundred thousand oblations of *arka* wood;
one obtains a thousand *dīnāra*s.
One should offer oblations of fresh butter;
one obtains five villages.
One should offer one hundred thousand oblations of *piṇḍāraka* flowers.
One obtains forty million pieces of fine cloth;
one should offer a hundred thousand oblations of milk,
whereby one obtains a hundred garments of *vitarka* silk.
One should offer one hundred thousand *kumuda* flowers;
one obtains a wife together with gold.
One should offer one hundred thousand *piṇḍāraka* flowers.
Having ascended a mountain peak, one should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times.
In whatever region one performs the recitation, the king of that region will attend upon one as a son.
One should offer oblations of lotuses marked with the syllable Śrī.
Padmaśrī approaches.
One who desires victory should constantly offer curd;
victory is then constant.
One desiring nourishment should offer oblations of clarified butter;
the attainment of wealth occurs. By one who is pure, [the results are achieved] constantly in five nights for a king, in seven nights for piśācas, and in nine nights for yakṣas and rākṣasas.
With the *dvāraśarātra* [rite], one subdues the Nāga kings; with half a month, the Gandharvas and Apsarases; with twenty-one days, the Devas, Dānavas, Asuras, Garuḍas, Kinnaras, and Divyas;
with twenty-four nights, all the Gaṇas; and with one month, one should offer eight thousand oblations of *rājapatnīvaśīkaraṇā*, *asurasamañjarī*, curd, honey, and ghee.
She becomes submissive.
One should offer one hundred thousand oblations of red karavīra buds;
one obtains a princess.
One should offer one hundred thousand oblations of bilva fruits smeared with bilva oil;
prosperity arises in the home.
One should offer one hundred thousand oblations of śatapuṣpā flowers smeared with curd.
One obtains one hundred dīnāras.
Having consecrated eight thousand pieces of black salt (*sauvarcala*) with mantras, one who has anointed their eyes brings all beings under control.
Having recited the mantra over perfumes, one should apply them as anointment.
The subjugation of all beings:
by reciting [the mantra] over one's form, one should fumigate oneself; this is the subjugation of all beings.
Having recited [the mantra], one should bind the topknot.
Protection everywhere;
the immobilization of all beings;
and for one desiring to bring a widow under control.
One should offer oblations of black gram (*māṣa*);
all will become submissive.
If one desires to bring a *yakṣiṇī* under control, one should offer eight thousand lotuses.
She arrives within three nights;
if she does not arrive then, she arrives within seven nights,
and she becomes a granter of boons.
One should seek according to one's desire.
One who desires a maiden should offer oblations a hundred thousand times;
he obtains the maiden of his choice.
Then, desiring to accomplish the Vetāla rite, one should take a corpse with its limbs unbroken to a cremation ground, or to a solitary tree, a crossroads, or a place with a single *liṅga*.
Having presented an offering (*bali*) consisting of all kinds of spirits, and having smeared a mandala before the right form of Mahādeva and offered the oblation there,
one should bathe and adorn [the corpse], draw a mandala with ashes, and [place it] in the center of it.
Having placed [the image] with its head to the east, the practitioner, covered by a white cloth and accompanied by friends dressed in white garments, should station the guardians of the directions.
Sitting upon a prepared seat, he should offer sesame and mustard seeds into its mouth until the jewel emerges from its mouth.

Having taken that [substance] and placed it in his own mouth, and having offered a bali-oblation for the prosperity of all beings, he stands before the Southern Form (Dakṣiṇamūrti). Taking yellow orpiment, red arsenic, collyrium, madder, and yellow pigment—these five together—and enclosing them between *aśvattha* leaves, he should recite the mantra until the threefold accomplishment occurs: it steams, smokes, and blazes. When it steams, one becomes a traveler on foot with a lifespan of five thousand years.
It brings all beings under one's control.
When it emits smoke, one becomes invisible and attains a lifespan of ten thousand years.
When it blazes with fire, one becomes a master of all vidyādharas.
The lord of all vidyādharas, remaining for an eon, reciting the mantra one hundred thousand times above [the image], becomes possessed of the five superknowledges (pañcābhijña).
He gains mastery over the binding of those above, below, and the guardians of the directions.
He becomes most beloved in the royal court.
He becomes one whose words are accepted.
One who desires a maiden should offer eight thousand *jātī* flowers;
he obtains a maiden.
By means of blossoming flowers, one obtains women;
or by means of the seal of all the grahas, through speech, a message, and yellow pigment (rocanā), one paralyzes fire and paralyzes ships.
She draws [the victim] near, whether bitten or unbitten, and causes possession;
she raises the dead and sends away fever by means of her voice.

Subsisting on milk and barley-gruel, having fasted for three nights and wearing clean garments, one should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times. Having placed [the deity] within the *liṅga* of the practitioner, and having performed a great worship, one should recite it an immeasurable number of times.
All children and the elderly will become submissive.
One may also fashion a bracelet with ashes over which the mantra has been empowered seven times.
One should cause water that has been empowered by reciting [the mantra] one hundred and eight times to be given to all beings;
it pacifies their diseases.

Having fasted for a day and night and fashioned a sword from *khadira* wood, one should recite [the mantra] in a cremation ground on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight until it blazes. By grasping it, one becomes a wielder of the sword-vidyā (*khaḍgavidyādhara*) with unimpeded movement.

One will have curled, ringlet-like hair, endure for an eon, and be highly esteemed by all the vidyādharas. Alternatively, having performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*) during an eclipse of the moon or sun, one should rise at dawn, perform worship of the cloth painting (*paṭa*), feed the monks,
and seek accomplishment (*siddhi*) together with ritual fees (*dakṣiṇā*).
Then, one becomes successful in even more difficult rites.
One should offer eight thousand oblations of young *dūrvā* grass shoots smeared with curds, honey, and ghee;
this releases from bondage. Furthermore, having consecrated a sword eight thousand times with mantras, one should place it at the entrance of a cave, a temple, or a city gate.
Having broken the door-panel, he tears open the door.
With a single recitation, there is protection for oneself.
By means of oblations of milk, women become submissive.
With the mind, one establishes the two mantras;
one paralyzes all mudrās and pulverizes all mantras.
One brings an asura maiden under control.

By offering a hundred oblations of all types of perfumes, women of noble family become submissive. By offering the remains of divine offerings (*devanirmālya*), goddesses, temple attendants (*taṭika*), and female renunciants (*pravrajitā*) become submissive.
Placing the hand upon the heart, one should recite;
this destroys all sins and attracts all sentient beings.
Placing the hand upon the head, one should recite.
One hundred and eight [times]:
this stuns all beings and destroys their sins.
Having recited [the mantra] over a wood-apple fruit (*bilva*), one attracts all beings.
In the practice of the *śikhā*, one should recite [the mantra] starting from the first day of the bright fortnight until sunset.
Then, having consecrated the crest-lock (*śikhā*) with eight thousand recitations,
one should go for alms at the houses of Brahmins.
When the giver of alms does not see [the practitioner], then it becomes accomplished.
On the first day, one alms-offering;
and so on for seven days.
On the twenty-first day, it succeeds even for one who lacks merit.
During a lunar eclipse, having recited the mantra over milk, one should drink it; it becomes a great elixir (*rasāyana*).
Having recited the mantra twenty-one times over a handful of water, if one throws it toward the house of someone, that person becomes submissive for seven days.
Having consecrated a handful of water seven times with mantras, whoever drinks it while reciting the name of another becomes subject to one's will.

By looking at someone while reciting the mantra twenty-one times, whoever is seen becomes subject to one's will. By performing one hundred thousand oblations of *guggulu* resin, one obtains a kingdom.
By offering or burning blue lotuses, white water lilies, red lotuses, and so forth, one brings whoever one desires under one's control.
With broken [fragments], a fire-wall is formed; or with pebbles in water, a crest-binding is made.
Taking natural collyrium and consecrating it twenty-one times, one should apply it;
one will become beloved by all people.
One should also anoint oneself with collyrium, tagara, kuṣṭha, vacā, lotus filaments, gorocanā, and elephant ichor, having empowered these eight substances with eight thousand recitations.
One becomes beloved by all.
Having fashioned an image out of salt, what do they do according to the previous ritual?
And having fashioned a jewel out of fresh butter and placed it upon four *aśvattha* leaves, one should recite the mantra until it emits steam.
One should swallow it without touching it with the teeth.
Immediately upon swallowing it, whatever one contemplates arises entirely.
One becomes able to assume any form at will and possesses the strength of ten men.
Having performed the preliminary practices for eighty thousand years, one should fast for three nights before a cloth painting on the full moon day;
having made offerings of incense, flowers, and so forth at a shrine containing relics, one should place a sword made of *kuśa* grass upon a lotus leaf and grasp it by the hilt.
One should recite the mantra until it vibrates.
Having taken [the substance], one becomes a vidyādhara.

In front of the cloth painting, during the fortnight of miracles (prātihārakapakṣa), bathing three times a day, changing clothes three times, and reciting the mantra eight thousand times at the three junctions of the day,
until the full moon.
Having fasted for three nights, one should prepare a *saṅghāṭī* robe, smear it with all types of perfumes, and light eight thousand ghee lamps.
Seated in the *paryaṅka* posture, having smeared a mandala with perfumes and placed the *saṅghāṭī* upon it,
one should press down on it with the left hand and recite the mantra until it flies up.
He stands at a height of seven palm trees.
Having paid homage to all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas with this very mantra, it should be taken up.
As soon as it is taken up, one becomes a Vidyādhara.
All the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, and others pay homage.

Having offered various oblations before the cloth painting and performed a grand worship, one should place *rocanā* on a lotus leaf and, seated in the *paryaṅka* posture, recite the mantra until the threefold accomplishment is attained.
When it becomes warm, there is the subjugation of all sentient beings, and one lives for a thousand years.
While it is smoking, he lives for thousands of millions of years;
he travels a thousand yojanas and returns to that very same place.
Unwearied among all the accomplished ones (siddhas), he becomes invisible by means of the mind;
he produces food by means of the mind;
then he blazes forth.

From the moment he first appears with the color of the sun, he becomes sixteen years of age, with hair curled and knotted like a *kuṇḍala*, remaining for an entire eon (*kalpa*), surrounded by hundreds of thousands of various *vidyādharas*, and going wherever he desires.

For one who has performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*), there are these signs: the movement of the flower garlands, the increasing of the lamp flame, the emission of rays of light, and the trembling of the cloth painting.
Having seen these, whatever he seeks to accomplish is achieved.
And there is the destruction of evil.

One who desires to bring under control the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas should kindle a fire with charcoal from khadira wood before the cloth painting and offer eight thousand oblations of salt, sesame seeds, and white mustard seeds smeared with curd, honey, and ghee, at the three junctions of the day for seven nights.
They become submissive.
Having consecrated water, ashes, or mustard seeds any one of these eight thousand times, one should scatter them in the four directions;
thus the binding of the mandala is accomplished.
One should offer eight thousand oblations of milk;
one will be liberated from disease.
One who desires food should offer oblations of food.
Having ascended a mountain peak, one who subsists on alms should recite [the mantra] three hundred thousand times.

At the conclusion, having fasted for three nights and kindled a fire with wood from the *aśvattha* tree, one should offer oblations of sesame seeds smeared with curd, honey, and ghee throughout the entire night;
one becomes a king.
By offering oblations of sesame and ghee, all aims are accomplished; one should offer honey, and one will become beloved by all people;
one should offer ghee.
If one offers milk as an oblation, one becomes radiant;
if one offers curd as an oblation, peace is attained.
Nourishment is attained.
Having kindled a fire with *sinduvāra* wood, one should offer the first portion of every cooked food;
thus, the prepared food becomes inexhaustible.
Whoever desires the binding of the turban obtains it;

one should offer a hundred thousand oblations of nimba flowers, and one becomes beloved by all people; one should offer a hundred thousand oblations of unbroken grains of śāli rice, and one obtains a village.
Having kindled a fire with *aśoka* wood, one should offer oblations a hundred thousand times;
one will obtain a kingdom in a single region.
While burning *agaru* incense before the cloth painting (*paṭa*), one should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times.
Then his royal palace comes under his control.
Subsisting on alms or sacrificial food, he should recite [the mantra] forty-nine hundred thousand times;
he obtains sovereignty over the earth.
Having subsisted on a diet of milk and barley gruel, one should recite [the mantra] eight hundred thousand times;
one should offer one hundred thousand white mustard seeds,
and one will obtain a neighboring kingdom.
One should offer a hundred thousand oblations of young durvā grass shoots;
one becomes long-lived.
One should offer a hundred thousand oblations of mango leaves smeared with milk.
One is liberated from all diseases.
Having gathered all kinds of grain in one place, one should offer them into the fire one hundred thousand times;
then all the grains become inexhaustible.
One should offer one hundred thousand oblations of Madhūka wood; wealth will arise.

Having combined realgar, yellow orpiment, and gallstone, and having consecrated the mixture eight thousand times in front of the cloth-painting, one should place it upon leaves from the wood of the Bodhi tree and recite the mantra.
It becomes effective;
whichever woman or man it is given to,
that person becomes submissive.
One should offer one hundred thousand oblations of clarified butter;
one obtains three villages. One should recite the mantra ten million times.
One becomes a vidyādhara with a retinue of one hundred;
by reciting [the mantra] one hundred thousand times,
one obtains delicious food and drink without having to ask for them.
The lord of the seven islands comes under one's control.
One should offer a hundred thousand oblations of *arka* wood;
there will be the binding of a royal turban.
One removes eye disease by means of the *apāmārjana* rite;
for one suffering from fever, there is the *apāmārjana* with *kuśa* grass. One should tie on a thread spun by a maiden that has been consecrated one hundred times with mantras.
One becomes fortunate.

Desiring to accomplish the ointment (*añjana*), one should take one *pala* of *sauvīrāñjana*, heat it with fire until it emits fragrance, and having purified the preliminary rites for the ointment, enter the water during a lunar eclipse and recite the mantra until the *kūṣmāṇḍa* [manifestation] appears.
At that very moment it bursts open;
as soon as it has burst open, this person becomes radiant,
wearing earrings and a crown, invincible to all vidyādharas, possessing unimpeded movement, and flies up together with his retinue.
One lives for five thousand years. If one offers a hundred thousand oblations of lotuses or blue lotuses,
one obtains a thousand pieces of gold.
One should offer one hundred thousand oblations of *palāśa* wood fuel;
one obtains a thousand pieces of gold.
Having fasted for three nights and subsisted on milk and barley gruel, one should perform the rite.
Taking one *pala* of realgar (*manaḥśilā*) and placing it upon seven leaves of the holy fig tree (*aśvattha*), one should recite the mantra until it bursts into flames.
One should then break open one's body and cast it [into the fire];
at that very moment, he rises up.

He becomes a Vidyādhara, possessing unimpeded divine, stainless ears and the speed of thought, with a complexion like the rising sun, highly esteemed by all Vidyādharas, moving through the divine realms, and accompanied by a retinue of a hundred Vidyādharas.
Having performed a grand worship with perfumes and flowers before the cloth painting, subsisting on milk and barley-gruel and wearing clean garments, whatever he prays for, that he obtains.

During a lunar eclipse, having performed worship beneath the Bodhi tree with perfumes, flowers, and incense, one should recite the mantra twenty-one times over realgar and yellow pigment (rocanā), then rub them upon the head. One should apply a tilaka mark on the forehead and enter the royal court.
One becomes a favorite of the king.
One should offer eight thousand oblations of lotus seeds smeared with curd, honey, and ghee;
whoever's name one takes during this rite, that person comes under one's control.
A celibate practitioner who has conquered his senses should perform a fire offering of agaru and turuṣka incense.
On the full moon day, he should bathe a king or one of royal rank with four jars filled with water that have been consecrated eight thousand times;
such a person becomes illustrious.
If she is not being cured, one should kindle a fire with milk-wood (*kṣīrasamidh*) and offer a hundred thousand oblations of the *vidyās* mixed with curds, honey, and ghee;
or alternatively, a *homa* may be performed with red and blue lotuses or *jātī* flowers.
Before the cloth painting (*paṭa*), one should subsist on a diet of milk and barley-gruel and perform ever-increasing worship.
The monks should be fed;
by this rite, even that which was unattainable becomes accomplished.
One who desires wealth obtains riches by performing a fire-oblation with *apāmārga* fuel-sticks.
Through oblations of ghee, rites for pacification and nourishment are accomplished;
or, by offering eight thousand lotuses smeared with curd, honey, and ghee, or oblations of ghee and guggulu,
all goals are likewise achieved.
He for whose sake an offering of *kṛṣṇavrīhi* rice is made after reciting the mantra becomes subject to one's will.
Subjugation is also achieved with fuel-sticks of *apāmārga*.
Having kindled a fire before the cloth-painting (*paṭa*) with wood of the *bilva* tree, one should offer one hundred thousand oblations of *agaru* (aloe) fuel-sticks.
It grants all objectives.
If one performs ten thousand oblations at a reliquary containing relics,
one obtains a kingdom.
By performing one hundred thousand *homa* offerings with lotuses, one becomes possessed of great wealth.
Before beginning any *homa*,
one should perform worship with perfumes, flowers, and incense.
Having kindled the fire with eight hundred *bilva* fuel-sticks, one should offer eight thousand oblations of *bilva* fuel-sticks smeared with curd, honey, and ghee.
Whomever one desires shall become submissive.
Having kindled the fire with milk-wood, one should offer one hundred thousand oblations of *agaru* (aloe) fuel-sticks.
It grants all goals.

Having performed worship with perfumes, flowers, and incense at a reliquary containing relics, one should rise early, become pure, kindle a fire, and offer eight thousand oblations of *nāgakesara* and *priyaṅgu*. Within a month, one obtains wealth.
Having kindled the fire with *palāśa* wood, one should offer oblations of *vaikaṅkata* fuel-sticks smeared with curds, honey, and ghee;
one will obtain a thousand gold pieces.
Alternatively, having kindled the fire with *udumbara* wood, one should offer one hundred thousand oblations of *vāṣaka* fuel-sticks smeared with curds, honey, and ghee.
Having consecrated it one hundred thousand times and bound it on the hand, one becomes invincible in battle.
By binding it on the head, one becomes invisible.
On the fifth day of the dark fortnight, having gone to a river, one should cause eight thousand white flowers to float away.
He obtains as much as eighty-eight thousand dīnāras;
this is the work of the *kunduruka*,
and this is also the work of the *bilva*.
It also bestows enjoyments.

On the fifth day of the dark fortnight, having fasted for a day and night before the cloth painting, one should place *gorocanā* on a white thread and recite the mantra until the threefold accomplishment is attained.
In the case of the "foot-walking" [accomplishment], one lives for seven thousand years.
When it blazes, one becomes a dweller for an eon (*kalpa*).
It effects the healing of all diseases;
with clay, it performs binding and releasing, as well as the binding of a mandala.
One should offer eight thousand oblations of lotuses before the cloth painting at the three junctions of the day for seven days;
one will see a treasure.
One should offer one hundred thousand oblations of *śatapuṣpā* flowers smeared with curd, honey, and ghee before the cloth painting.
One obtains a territory;
one should offer a hundred thousand oblations of clarified butter,
and one obtains five villages.
One should offer eight thousand oblations of *arka* flowers;
one obtains a thousand gold coins (*rūpaka*).
While the mantra is being recited, it grants everything.
Excluding anything associated with sensual desire,

one who has fasted for the night on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight should, during the night, offer ten thousand oblations of discarded flower garlands smeared with curds, honey, and ghee before the noble Mañjuśrī;
he will obtain great prosperity.
Beneath a Bodhi tree, one should offer eight thousand oblations of Bodhi-tree wood;
one will obtain a thousand pieces of gold.
One should offer eight thousand *jāti* flowers three times a day for seven nights.
One obtains a thousand gold coins.

By performing these rites while fasting for three nights, one should kindle a fire beneath a Bodhi tree with fuel sticks of milk-tree wood and offer eight thousand pills of *guggulu* resin, each the size of a cotton seed;
one then obtains a thousand *dīnāra* coins.
For eye diseases, fever, abdominal tumors, headaches, and sciatica, one should recite [the mantra] over [the medicine] and administer it.

For protection against wolves, tigers, buffaloes, crocodiles, elephants, thieves, serpents, piśācas, bhūtas, and brahmarākṣasas, as well as from all fears and calamities arising from aquatic creatures, one should provide protection by means of this very [mantra].
Having gone to a lotus pond, one should offer one hundred thousand lotuses.
One obtains a common kingship.

Having performed the preliminary rites (*puraścara�na*), one should take realgar (*manaḥśilā*) and grind it with human milk. Having offered a thousand oblations (*sahasrasampātāhuti*), while observing the *poṣadha* fast, one should form five pills, place them in a casket made of agallochum (*agaru*), together with white mustard seeds (*siddhārtha*).

During a lunar eclipse or a solar eclipse, having performed the offering of bali, one should place [the substance] in a casket before the painted image and recite the mantra until the mustard seeds crackle;
at that time, it effects the subjugation of all sentient beings.
If it smokes, one becomes the king of all those who possess the power of invisibility and lives for infinite eons;
if, moreover, it blazes forth, [one attains even greater results].
Then, possessing a radiance equal to the rising sun, he becomes a king of the Vidyādharas who remains for a great eon (mahākalpa).
Rocanā, haritāla, and other such substances are to be accomplished by this very same procedure;
for all of them, there are three kinds of accomplishment.
One who desires to bring about peace should have the sacrificial fire kindled with fuel-sticks by officiating priests and offer eight thousand oblations of *paramānna* for three nights;
peace will be attained.
For oneself or another, or for a village or city in the event of drought, one should offer the "three sweets" (*trimadhura*) for seven nights.
Having consecrated the conch, banner, and other objects with mantras, one exhausts [the effects of] karma;
within seven days, one exhausts even the five sins of immediate retribution and becomes capable of performing all ritual actions.
A binding of knowledge should be made with a thread over which the mantra has been recited twenty-one times;
a binding of the mandala should be performed with mustard seeds during a lunar eclipse or a solar eclipse.

Alternatively, having smeared a mandala with sandalwood paste, one should place equal portions of ghee, honey, and *āmalakī* juice in a copper vessel; then, sitting in the cross-legged posture (*paryaṅka*), one should recite the mantra until it becomes warm.
Having drunk that, one becomes a possessor of a retentive memory (*śrutidhara*).
One who observes the *poṣadha* vows should, at the improper time, recite the mantra seven times over a mouthful of water and drink it.
Having contemplated whatever one intends to do, one speaks of it even in a dream.
Having recited the white *vacā* root seven times and placed it between the teeth in the mouth, whatever one requests is obtained;
one becomes a superior debater.
Whatever state of being one has in mind while reciting, having offered flowers, incense, and so forth before the Tathāgata, one should cast offerings for the directions toward the four quarters.
Then, seated upon a bundle of *kuśa* grass, one should recite [the mantra] eight thousand times;
this fulfills all hopes.

Having fashioned a lion out of anthill clay and anointed it with *gorocanā*, one who has performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*) should prepare a ritual ball (*piṇḍaka*), place it before the cloth painting, and recite the mantra three hundred thousand times.
Then it moves;
as soon as it moves, one becomes accomplished (*siddha*).
At that very moment, while reciting the mantra, one should mount the lion;
with hair curled in locks, having the appearance of a sixteen-year-old—though being the sixteenth year of one's own life—one flies up.
Having arrived among all the *vidyādharas*, possessing the lifespan of Brahmā, and upon death, one is reborn among the gods.
Upon seeing or hearing of an enemy army, one should paralyze it.
Having filled a jar with water scented with all types of rice and having covered its mouth with mango sprouts, one should bathe the Vināyaka with that jar empowered by eight thousand recitations;
he will quickly release [the obstruction].
One should bathe a pregnant woman;
she will give birth with ease.
One should bathe the infant.
One becomes liberated from all planetary influences;
by this consecration, one becomes completely liberated and becomes equal to the [accomplished] practitioner.

To subjugate a great feudal lord (mahāsāmanta), one should offer eight thousand oblations of *arka* wood fuel smeared with curd, honey, and ghee before a painted image for seven nights at the three junctions of the day;
he, together with his retinue, will become submissive.
To win a princess, one should offer eight thousand oblations of *priyaṅgu* flowers for seven days to whomever she is to be given.
One should offer oblations of oil-cake and wood eight thousand times at the three junctions of the day for seven nights;
this brings even those standing before one under control.
Having performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*), one should subsist on alms and recite the mantra one hundred thousand times at a reliquary (*caitya*) containing relics.

Then, on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, having fasted for one night and performed worship of the cloth-painting according to one's means, one should offer eight thousand oblations of black sesame seeds smeared with curd, honey, and ghee.
Then, at dawn, one obtains a village;
[if repeated], twelve.
If the ritual actions have not yet been accomplished, one obtains a village with a thousand households.

Having performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*), one should set up the cloth painting (*paṭa*) on the bank of a river facing west; subsisting on water and barley-meal, having performed worship according to one's means, and having lit twenty-one lamps of ghee, one should offer an oblation (*bali*) to all spirits outside.
Having made the offering, one should sit in the paryanka posture and recite the mantra until Aruṇa, the son of a god, arrives;
he then grants a boon.
One should subsist on alms and recite for three months beneath a vaṭa tree.
Then, on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, having smeared a sacrificial ground (*sthaṇḍila*) the size of a cow-hide and offered a *bali* consisting of all flavors,

and having given a *bali* for all spirits outside, one should sit upon a bundle of *kuśa* grass and offer eight thousand oblations of *guggulu* resin pills, each the size of a jujube seed, into smokeless embers. Then the Yakṣiṇī Paṭavāsinī arrives.
One should offer her the *argha* with scented water.
She asks, "What shall I do?"—among these options, one should choose her as mother, sister, or friend.
She then bestows the elixir of flavors (*rasarasāyana*).
Having consumed that, one attains a lifespan of an eon and gains the strength of a yakṣa.

Having performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*), having made offerings according to one's means at a shrine containing relics (*sadhātuka-caitya*), bathing three times a day, and reciting the *aparimita* mantra at the three junctions of the day for six months, [the goal is attained].
Subsisting on alms-food or a diet of milk and barley-gruel,
one should then begin the practice.

During the dark fortnight, under the Puṣya asterism, having purchased red oleander (*karavīra*) and realgar (*manaḥśilā*) from a hero-seller, one should [wash them] with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*).

Having purified a Brahmin girl, given her a left-hand medicinal herb, and having had her bathe and adorned herself, one should enter facing east and grind [the herb] during an auspicious lunar day, karana, and muhurta.
Having formed an uneven pill the size of a jujube stone with the ring finger, one should place it inside a casket made of *aśvattha* wood.

Having performed a thousand oblations before the cloth painting and fasted for seven nights, at the end of that period during the bright fortnight, one should perform a magnificent worship and present an even more magnificent *bali* offering.

Having prepared a casket honored with perfumes, flowers, and incense, and having placed it upon four *aśvattha* leaves and covered it with three more, one should hold it firmly with the hand while [reciting] for all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas...
Having performed a prostration and sat upon a bundle of *kuśa* grass,
one should recite the mantra until substances such as elixirs and alchemical potions appear;
then, one departs once again.
Half [of it] should be used for the Three Jewels;
then, if one remains right there,
there will be no fear of the discus of Viṣṇu.
One sees the Blessed Maitreya;
having made a vow, one should enter.
This is the warding off of all obstacles.
In a clean place, one should cast a house of dust upon mustard seeds;
all obstacles will be warded off,
and one will attain swift passage.
One should say, "Go!
Having fashioned an earthen seal upon the hem of a garment and empowered it eight thousand times, one should place it upon the bitten person and summon [the poison];
even a dead person will rise up.

Having purified substances such as realgar (*manaḥśilā*) and so forth, or weapons such as the sword, discus, and *musuṇḍī* with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*), and having performed a thousand oblations (*sahasrasampātāhuti*),

one should take one of those substances, draw the practice maṇḍala on a cloth on the full moon day, place the substance upon it, sit in the cross-legged posture (*paryaṅka*), and recite [the mantra] until success (*siddhi*) is attained.
Having written the name of whatever object one desires upon a wooden board and having empowered it with eight thousand recitations of the mantra, it should be thrown into a lake where a nāga resides.
That nāga will provide everything;
within seven days, he will certainly provide the desired thing.
Having written the name of the desired object upon a wooden plank, one should likewise cast it into a well or a lake along with wealth and other items;
then, a man should be made to submerge into the water. He hears a great sound from within that [water].
"In such-and-such a place, wealth and other goods remain;
they should be taken from there.
This should be remembered at river crossings and the like, as well as in the ten [cases], in an assembly, in the royal court, or in a dispute.
One becomes invincible everywhere.
If one wishes to bring someone under one's control, one should visualize Noble Mañjuśrī in that person’s mouth and engage in some conversation;
before long, they will come under one's influence.
Having placed water in a vessel, one should meditate upon Noble Mañjuśrī.
With that water, over which the mantra has been recited eight thousand times, one should contemplate the bitten person;
he becomes free from poison.

Having entered the maṇḍala according to the prescribed rite, one who subsists on sacrificial food (haviṣya) and maintains silence should take cow-dung that has not fallen [to the ground] from a complete bull, construct a maṇḍala, and recite [the mantra] starting from the full moon until he has recited it a third time, reaching one hundred thousand repetitions (lakṣa). Observing celibacy, he should perform this vow for six months.
Success is attained here in one month;
after six months, the black world becomes manifest to him.
He also attains supreme accomplishment even with his physical body.
In brief, one accomplishes all mantras.
From the *Mahākalparāja*, the *Āryamañjuśrīmūlakalpa*, the fifty-fifth chapter,
the section on the accomplishment of gold, is concluded in its full extent and detail.
And thus concludes the ritual manual (kalpa) of the noble Mañjuśrī as it was obtained.

Hail! Written on the [blank] day of the bright fortnight of Mārgaśīrṣa, under the lunar mansion Padā, while Jupiter was situated in Leo, by the scholar Ravicandra—who has come from the Middle Country and is the presiding master of the illustrious Mūlaghoṣa Monastery, [and who is known as] Śrībo...—the Mañjuśrī-kalpa is completed. May there be auspiciousness! May it be virtuous!
